item.content:encoded:
The Oxford Centre for Emerging Minds Research (OCEMR) DPhil Studentships 2027 offer an exceptional opportunity for prospective doctoral researchers who want to contribute to cutting-edge research focused on children and young people, neurodiversity, mental health, development, learning, and well-being.

For the 2027 entry cycle, the Oxford Centre for Emerging Minds Research is inviting expressions of interest from candidates interested in undertaking a DPhil at the University of Oxford from October 2027. Thanks to generous funding from the Paul Foundation, up to four fully funded studentships are available.

The funding package includes a stipend and fees for three years at the UK home-fee rate, with the funded studentships expected to be completed by October 2030. The opportunity is particularly relevant to researchers interested in understanding children’s and young people’s differences, strengths, development, and mental health, while contributing to research designed to promote more inclusive and supportive environments.

According to the Department of Experimental Psychology, the Oxford Centre for Emerging Minds Research focuses on conducting world-class research with children and young people, with the broader goal of creating a world in which differences are understood and accepted, individual strengths are recognised and developed, and mental health difficulties are prevented or addressed at an early stage.

Oxford Centre for Emerging Minds Research DPhil Studentships 2027

The University of Oxford is one of the world’s leading research universities, and the OCEMR provides an interdisciplinary research environment bringing together expertise relevant to child development, mental health, psychology, and related fields.

The 2027 studentships are designed for candidates who want to pursue doctoral-level research within the Centre and contribute to research that has potential implications for children, young people, families, educators, and other stakeholders.

The Centre’s research agenda is particularly concerned with:

  • Children and young people’s development
  • Mental health and well-being
  • Neurodiversity
  • Understanding individual differences
  • Strengths-based approaches
  • Learning and development
  • Early identification and prevention of mental health difficulties
  • Inclusive approaches to childhood and adolescence
  • Research involving children, young people, and their families
  • Interdisciplinary approaches to psychological and developmental research

What Does the Oxford OCEMR DPhil Studentship 2027 Cover?

One of the most attractive aspects of this opportunity is its funding package.

The University of Oxford states that up to four fully funded OCEMR studentships will be offered for the October 2027 intake.

Successful students will receive:

  • A doctoral studentship for three years
  • A stipend for living expenses
  • University fees at the UK home-fee rate
  • The opportunity to undertake doctoral research within the Oxford Centre for Emerging Minds Research
  • Membership of an interdisciplinary research environment
  • The opportunity to work alongside researchers with expertise in children, young people, psychology, education, and mental health
  • The opportunity to contribute to research with potential practical and societal impact

The funding is supported by the Paul Foundation. Because of the structure of the funding, the studentships are expected to be completed by October 2030.

Important Note About the Funding

Applicants should pay particular attention to the fact that the published funding is specified at the UK home-fee rate.

This means applicants should carefully examine the University’s graduate admissions and funding requirements to determine how their individual fee status affects the total financial support available to them.

The department also notes that scholarship and grant opportunities for UK study can be highly competitive and may have specific nationality, course, or eligibility restrictions. Prospective applicants are therefore encouraged to check the detailed eligibility requirements before applying.

Who Is the Oxford OCEMR DPhil Opportunity For?

The opportunity is intended for prospective doctoral researchers who have a strong interest in research involving children and young people and whose academic interests align with the Centre’s research priorities.

Potential applicants may be particularly well-suited to the opportunity if their interests involve areas such as the following:

  1. Child development
  2. Adolescent development
  3. Psychology
  4. Mental health
  5. Neurodiversity
  6. Autism
  7. ADHD
  8. Learning and education
  9. Language and communication
  10. Executive functions and self-regulation
  11. Socio-emotional development
  12. Wellbeing
  13. Strengths-based approaches
  14. Inclusive research
  15. Assistive technology
  16. Artificial intelligence and its application to developmental or educational research
  17. Community-based participatory research
  18. Co-production with children, young people, families, and educators

The opportunity is therefore broader than a conventional psychology PhD. The Centre’s work brings together psychological, clinical, educational, and developmental perspectives, making it particularly attractive to candidates whose research interests cross disciplinary boundaries.

Research Themes Within the Oxford Centre for Emerging Minds Research

The Oxford Centre for Emerging Minds Research is focused on research that can improve understanding of children’s and young people’s experiences and support better developmental and mental health outcomes.

Its work is centred around the principle that differences between people should be understood and accepted, while strengths should be recognised and supported.

The Centre also aims to address mental health difficulties through prevention and early intervention rather than waiting until problems become more severe.

This makes the DPhil opportunity especially relevant for researchers interested in research that connects academic investigation with real-world challenges affecting children, young people, and their communities.

What Kind of Research Could Applicants Pursue?

The source material indicates that applicants will be able to consider potential OCEMR DPhil projects and should consult the available project information when developing their expression of interest.

The Centre’s research direction includes work examining the following:

  • How children’s and young people’s strengths can be identified and supported
  • How differences in development influence learning and well-being
  • How mental health difficulties can be prevented or addressed early
  • How neurodivergent children and young people can be better supported
  • How families and educators can contribute to research
  • How research can incorporate the perspectives of children and young people
  • How interdisciplinary methods can be used to address complex developmental questions

Candidates should therefore avoid approaching the application as simply an opportunity to study a broad topic. A strong application should demonstrate a clear intellectual connection between the applicant’s research interests and the Centre’s research priorities.

Why This DPhil Opportunity Is Significant

A doctoral studentship at Oxford provides more than financial support. It provides an opportunity to develop advanced research expertise in an internationally recognised academic environment.

For candidates interested in child development, mental health, psychology, neurodiversity, or related areas, the OCEMR provides an environment where research can be connected to broader questions concerning education, well-being, inclusion, and social development.

The Centre’s emphasis on interdisciplinary research can also allow doctoral researchers to engage with perspectives beyond a single academic discipline.

Application Timeline and Deadline

The deadline for initial expressions of interest is 12.00 noon on Tuesday, 22 September 2026.

Key Dates

  • Application stage: Initial expression of interest
  • Deadline: Tuesday, 22 September 2026
  • Time: 12.00 noon
  • DPhil start: October 2027
  • Expected completion: October 2030

Applicants should not wait until the final day to prepare their materials. Doctoral applications often require substantial preparation, including reviewing research projects, identifying academic fit and preparing supporting documents.

How to Apply for the Oxford OCEMR DPhil Studentships 2027

The first stage is to submit an expression of interest for the OCEMR DPhil opportunity.

The Department of Experimental Psychology provides information about potential OCEMR DPhil projects and separate guidance concerning the submission of an expression of interest.

Prospective candidates should, therefore:

Step 1: Review the Available Research Projects

Begin by examining the available OCEMR DPhil projects.

This is important because doctoral research at Oxford is expected to demonstrate a strong connection between the applicant’s proposed interests and the academic expertise available within the department and research centre.

Step 2: Assess Your Academic and Research Fit

Consider whether your academic background, previous research experience, and proposed interests align with the Centre’s areas of research.

Applicants should be able to explain why the OCEMR is the appropriate environment for their doctoral research.

Step 3: Develop a Clear Research Direction

Your expression of interest should demonstrate intellectual curiosity and a clear understanding of the research area you want to investigate.

Rather than presenting an extremely broad topic, applicants should identify a research direction that can realistically be developed into doctoral research.

Step 4: Prepare the Required Application Materials

Applicants should carefully follow the University’s instructions concerning the expression of interest and submit the requested materials before the deadline.

The source specifically provides a separate document containing information about submitting the expression of interest.

Step 5: Submit Before the Deadline

The initial expression of interest must be submitted by:

12.00 noon, Tuesday, 22 September 2026.

Late applications may not be considered, so applicants should allow sufficient time to complete the process.

APPLY HERE

What Makes a Strong Applicant?

Although the source does not provide a single comprehensive checklist of all selection criteria for the 2027 OCEMR studentships, prospective candidates should demonstrate a strong alignment with the Centre’s research agenda.

A competitive applicant would ideally be able to demonstrate:

  • Strong academic preparation
  • Clear research interests
  • Interest in children and young people
  • Alignment with the Centre’s research priorities
  • An ability to think critically about research questions
  • Potential to conduct independent doctoral research
  • Interest in interdisciplinary research
  • A commitment to research that can contribute to improved understanding of development, wellbeing or mental health
  • A clear reason for wanting to undertake doctoral study at Oxford

Previous research experience can also be valuable when demonstrating preparedness for doctoral-level study, although applicants should rely on the official admissions and studentship guidance for the precise requirements.

International Applicants and Eligibility

The available source does not state that the 2027 OCEMR studentships are restricted to a particular race, nationality, or continent.

However, the funding information explicitly states that the three-year funding package covers fees at the UK home-fee rate. Applicants from outside the UK should therefore carefully review the University’s rules concerning overseas fee status and funding before applying.

The Department of Experimental Psychology also cautions that funding schemes can have different nationality and course restrictions, making it important for international candidates to confirm their eligibility for the specific funding arrangement.

Why Applicants Should Start Early

The September 2026 deadline provides applicants with limited time to prepare a high-quality doctoral expression of interest.

Candidates should use the available preparation period to:

  1. Research the Oxford Centre for Emerging Minds Research.
  2. Review the available DPhil projects.
  3. Identify the research themes that most closely match their academic interests.
  4. Review the University’s graduate admissions requirements.
  5. Examine the relevant fee and funding conditions.
  6. Prepare a strong academic CV.
  7. Develop their research interests into a focused doctoral direction.
  8. Review any required supporting documents.
  9. Ensure that their application demonstrates a clear fit with the proposed research environment.
  10. Submit the expression of interest before the stated deadline.

The Wider Funding Landscape at Oxford

The Department of Experimental Psychology states that applicants who receive an offer are automatically considered for funding from a number of sources, including the Wellcome Trust, MRC, BBSRC, Cancer Research UK, ESRC, the British Heart Foundation, the Clarendon Fund, Oxford colleges, and various charitable sources.

The department advises applicants seeking funding for its graduate courses to submit their university applications by the early December deadline.

This broader funding landscape demonstrates why prospective students should investigate multiple funding routes rather than relying on a single studentship.

Oxford also provides a funding search tool intended to help applicants identify scholarships, studentships, and awards for which they may be eligible.

Career and Academic Benefits of a Funded DPhil

Completing a funded DPhil at the University of Oxford can provide substantial academic and professional development.

Potential benefits include the following:

  • Advanced doctoral research training
  • Development of specialist expertise
  • Experience conducting independent research
  • Exposure to interdisciplinary research
  • Collaboration with researchers from different fields
  • Opportunities to contribute to research publications and outputs
  • Development of analytical and methodological skills
  • Experience working on research involving children and young people
  • Preparation for academic and research careers
  • Development of expertise relevant to psychology, education, mental health, policy, and related fields
  • Membership of an internationally recognised academic research environment

For individuals pursuing careers in academia, research, public policy, education, mental health, or child development, this type of doctoral training can provide a strong foundation for future professional opportunities.

How to Make Your Application More Competitive

Applicants should focus on research fit, academic preparation, and intellectual clarity.

A strong expression of interest should communicate more than the desire to study at Oxford. It should explain why the applicant’s research interests belong within the OCEMR environment.

1. Demonstrate a Clear Research Interest

Explain the research problem you are interested in exploring and why it matters.

2. Connect Your Interests to OCEMR

Show how your proposed research connects with the Centre’s work on children, young people, development, mental health, neurodiversity, and well-being.

3. Demonstrate Research Potential

Highlight previous research projects, dissertations, publications, research assistantships, fieldwork, methodological training, or other relevant experiences where applicable.

4. Show Interdisciplinary Thinking

Many challenges affecting children and young people cannot be addressed through a single discipline. Demonstrating an ability to connect psychology with education, mental health, technology, communication, or other relevant fields can strengthen the intellectual case for your research.

5. Be Specific

Avoid overly broad statements such as wanting to “improve children’s mental health.” Instead, identify the particular research problem, population, developmental stage, mechanism, or intervention that interests you.

6. Explain the Potential Contribution

Consider what your research could add to existing knowledge and how it might ultimately contribute to children, young people, families, educators, or practitioners.

Important Advice for Prospective Applicants

The Department of Experimental Psychology explicitly advises prospective applicants to check eligibility requirements carefully because scholarships and grants can have strict conditions relating to nationality and courses.

Applicants should therefore avoid assuming that being academically qualified automatically means they qualify for every available funding scheme.

In particular, international applicants should carefully investigate:

  • Their fee status
  • Whether the stated funding covers their applicable fees
  • Graduate admission requirements
  • Studentship-specific eligibility requirements
  • Any nationality restrictions
  • Required application deadlines
  • Research project requirements

Contact for Informal Enquiries

For informal enquiries concerning the Oxford Centre for Emerging Minds Research DPhil studentships, the department provides the following contact:

Email: ocemr@psy.ox.ac.uk

Applicants with questions about research fit or the available projects should use the appropriate official contact channels and consult the University’s published application guidance.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Oxford OCEMR DPhil Studentship?

It is a funded doctoral research opportunity within the Oxford Centre for Emerging Minds Research at the University of Oxford, focusing on research involving children and young people, including areas related to development, mental health, neurodiversity, and wellbeing.

How many studentships are available?

The University states that up to four fully funded OCEMR studentships are available for October 2027 entry.

How long is the funding?

The studentships provide funding for three years.

What does the funding cover?

The funding provides a stipend and fees for three years at the UK home-fee rate.

When does the DPhil begin?

The studentships are for candidates undertaking DPhil study from October 2027.

When is the deadline?

The deadline for the initial expression of interest is 12.00 noon on Tuesday, 22 September 2026.

Who can apply?

The opportunity is aimed at candidates seeking doctoral research opportunities within the Oxford Centre for Emerging Minds Research. Applicants should have research interests aligned with the Centre’s work involving children and young people.

Can international applicants apply?

The source does not state a race or continent restriction. However, because the funding is specified at the UK home-fee rate, international candidates should carefully verify their fee status and the precise funding arrangements before applying.

What research areas are relevant?

Relevant interests include child and adolescent development, mental health, neurodiversity, autism, ADHD, learning, communication, well-being, strengths-based approaches, and related areas.

Where can applicants find more information?

The Department of Experimental Psychology provides links to information about potential OCEMR DPhil projects and guidance on submitting the expression of interest.

Visit HERE for more information about the Oxford Centre for Emerging Minds Research DPhil Studentships 2027.

Final Thoughts

The Oxford Centre for Emerging Minds Research DPhil Studentships 2027 represent a significant opportunity for aspiring doctoral researchers who want to contribute to research addressing some of the most important questions surrounding childhood, adolescence, neurodiversity, mental health, development, and wellbeing.

With up to four fully funded studentships, three years of funding, a stipend, and fees at the UK home-fee rate, the opportunity offers successful candidates the chance to undertake doctoral research within one of the world’s most prestigious academic environments.

The Centre’s emphasis on understanding differences, recognising strengths and preventing or addressing mental health difficulties early makes the opportunity particularly relevant to researchers who want their work to have both academic and societal relevance.

Prospective applicants should begin preparing early, carefully review the available research projects, assess their academic and research fit, and pay close attention to the funding and admissions requirements. Most importantly, candidates should remember that the initial expression of interest deadline is 12:00 noon on Tuesday, 22 September 2026.

For anyone seeking a fully funded doctoral opportunity at Oxford in the fields of child development, psychology, neurodiversity, mental health, and wellbeing, the OCEMR DPhil Studentships 2027 are an opportunity worth serious consideration.

item.content:encoded:
The International Development Innovation Alliance (IDIA) Academy Adaptive Leadership Programme 2026 is now accepting applications from development professionals and innovation leaders seeking to strengthen their ability to manage innovation, navigate complex development challenges and scale solutions for sustainable impact.

The Managing Innovation for Impact Adaptive Leadership Programme 2026 will take place from 7–10 December 2026 in Ghana and will bring together a cohort of 24 participants for an intensive learning and networking experience.

The programme is designed for professionals working across development innovation, philanthropy, investment, civil society and multilateral organisations. It combines structured learning, personal reflection and collaborative networking to help participants develop the leadership capabilities, practical tools and professional networks needed to drive innovation and achieve impact.

Applications are open from 5 August to 28 August 2026.

IDIA Academy Adaptive Leadership Programme 2026 Overview

Opportunity Details
Programme IDIA Academy Managing Innovation for Impact Adaptive Leadership Programme 2026
Organiser International Development Innovation Alliance (IDIA) Academy
Dates 7–10 December 2026
Location Ghana
Duration 4 days
Cohort Size 24 places
Application Period 5–28 August 2026
Deadline 28 August 2026
Programme Fee USD $2,495
Scholarships Limited fully subsidised IDIA scholarships available
Scholarship Focus Individuals from the Global South
Target Participants Development practitioners, innovation leaders, funders and decision-makers
Format Immersive professional development programme
Application Online application form

What Is the IDIA Academy?

The International Development Innovation Alliance Academy, commonly referred to as the IDIA Academy, provides professional development opportunities designed to strengthen the capabilities of people working in international development and innovation.

The Academy equips development practitioners, funders and decision-makers with strategies, frameworks and practical tools for identifying, designing and scaling solutions to complex global challenges.

Its training portfolio covers different aspects of development innovation and is designed to respond to emerging needs within the international development sector.

The Academy’s programmes can include immersive training courses delivered in different countries as well as specialised programmes addressing particular sectors and development contexts.

The IDIA Academy has also expanded its training portfolio to include artificial intelligence, helping development innovation leaders understand practical frameworks, tools and skills for the responsible and inclusive use of AI-driven technologies in development.

What Is the Managing Innovation for Impact Adaptive Leadership Programme?

The Managing Innovation for Impact Adaptive Leadership Programme 2026 is designed to help development innovation leaders become more effective at navigating complex challenges and leading innovation for sustainable impact.

Development challenges are often complex, interconnected and constantly changing. Traditional leadership approaches may not always be sufficient when organisations are attempting to scale innovative solutions, influence systems or work across multiple stakeholders.

The Adaptive Leadership Programme addresses this challenge by combining:

  • Structured learning
  • Leadership development
  • Personal reflection
  • Systems thinking
  • Innovation principles
  • Storytelling
  • Collaborative networking
  • Practical application
  • Peer learning

The programme is intended to help participants develop the mindset and practical capabilities required to lead innovation in environments where uncertainty, complexity and change are common.

Key Objectives of the Programme

The programme seeks to help participants become more capable and confident leaders of innovation.

Participants will explore approaches that can help them understand complex development problems, identify opportunities for innovation and support the scaling of solutions that can create meaningful impact.

The programme focuses on developing both knowledge and practical leadership capacity, allowing participants to take what they learn and apply it within their organisations and professional environments.

What Will Participants Gain?

Participants who complete the IDIA Academy training are expected to benefit from enhanced leadership capacity, increased confidence and efficacy, and access to a lifelong professional network.

1. Enhanced Leadership Capacity

One of the central benefits of the programme is the opportunity to strengthen leadership capabilities related to innovation and impact.

Participants will gain knowledge of important innovation principles and systems-thinking concepts that can help them understand complex development environments.

The training also introduces storytelling techniques that can help leaders communicate their ideas, strategies and innovation priorities more effectively.

This can be particularly valuable for professionals who need to convince internal teams, funders, policymakers or external stakeholders to support new approaches.

Participants can use these capabilities to:

  • Develop innovation strategies.
  • Communicate organisational priorities.
  • Understand complex systems.
  • Identify opportunities for innovation.
  • Support innovation portfolios.
  • Develop approaches for scaling impact.
  • Influence stakeholders.
  • Lead organisational change.

2. Increased Confidence and Effectiveness

The programme is also designed to improve participants’ confidence and effectiveness as leaders.

According to the programme information, training alumni report significant growth in their ability to lead and inspire change, collaborate with others and apply practical tools in real-world situations.

This means the programme goes beyond theoretical learning.

Participants are expected to engage with practical approaches that can be applied to the challenges they encounter in their organisations and professional roles.

The ability to confidently navigate complex situations can be particularly valuable for innovation leaders working in environments where there is no single straightforward solution.

3. A Lifelong Global Network

Another major component of the programme is its international professional network.

IDIA Academy programmes bring together diverse cohorts of professionals working across different areas of development, innovation, investment, philanthropy, civil society and other related fields.

Participants have the opportunity to build relationships with professionals who may have different experiences, perspectives and areas of expertise.

These relationships can continue beyond the programme and provide opportunities for:

  • Professional collaboration.
  • Knowledge sharing.
  • Peer learning.
  • Resource sharing.
  • Future partnerships.
  • Collective action.
  • Continued professional development.

For professionals working in international development, having a diverse global network can be an important career and collaboration asset.

Who Is the Programme Designed For?

The IDIA Academy Managing Innovation for Impact Adaptive Leadership Programme is open to individuals who are motivated to advance innovation for sustainable development.

The programme specifically identifies professionals working across a range of organisations and sectors, including:

  • Multilateral agencies
  • Philanthropic organisations
  • Investment funds
  • Civil society organisations
  • Development organisations
  • Innovation-focused institutions

The programme is particularly relevant to people whose responsibilities involve developing, managing, financing or influencing innovation.

Professionals Particularly Encouraged to Apply

IDIA particularly encourages applications from individuals who perform responsibilities such as the following.

Innovation Portfolio Managers

Professionals who manage innovation portfolios can benefit from learning approaches for assessing, supporting and scaling innovative solutions.

This may include individuals responsible for overseeing multiple innovation initiatives or programmes within an organisation.

Scaling Programme Managers

The programme is also relevant to professionals responsible for scaling programmes or innovations.

Scaling innovation requires more than identifying a promising idea. It involves understanding systems, stakeholders, resources, institutional environments and the factors that influence adoption.

Professionals working on scaling initiatives can therefore use the programme to strengthen their leadership and strategic capabilities.

Country Innovation Ecosystem Influencers

Individuals who influence innovation ecosystem strategies at country level are also specifically encouraged to apply.

These professionals may work with governments, development agencies, civil society organisations, funders or other stakeholders to strengthen national innovation systems.

Institutional Innovation Policy Leaders

The programme is relevant to people involved in shaping institutional innovation policies.

Such professionals may be responsible for creating policies, strategies or organisational approaches that enable innovation.

Innovation Investors

Individuals who invest in innovations addressing global development challenges are another important target group.

This can include professionals working in investment funds, philanthropy or other funding institutions that support innovative approaches to development challenges.

Programme Content and Learning Approach

The Adaptive Leadership Programme uses a combination of learning methods rather than relying exclusively on traditional classroom instruction.

The programme incorporates structured learning, personal reflection and collaborative networking.

This approach is intended to help participants understand innovation concepts while also reflecting on their own leadership approaches and learning from peers.

Structured Learning

Participants are introduced to frameworks, concepts and tools relevant to innovation and adaptive leadership.

Personal Reflection

Participants have opportunities to reflect on their own leadership approaches, professional challenges and organisational contexts.

Reflection can help professionals understand how they respond to uncertainty, complexity and organisational change.

Collaborative Networking

The programme brings together professionals from different backgrounds, enabling participants to learn from one another and explore potential areas of collaboration.

This peer-learning component can be particularly valuable because development innovation often requires collaboration between organisations and sectors.

Why Adaptive Leadership Matters in Development Innovation

Global development challenges frequently involve multiple interconnected factors.

Issues such as poverty, climate change, health systems, inequality, food security and institutional development cannot always be solved through one intervention or one organisation.

Innovation leaders therefore need to understand the broader systems within which their interventions operate.

Adaptive leadership can help professionals respond to changing circumstances, work with different stakeholders and adjust strategies when circumstances change.

The IDIA Academy programme is therefore particularly relevant to professionals who are responsible for leading innovation in complex environments.

Programme Location and Dates

The 2026 programme will be held in Ghana.

Programme Dates

7–10 December 2026

The training will therefore take place over four days.

Participants should take the programme dates into consideration when applying and make sure they will be able to participate fully if selected.

Programme Cohort

The programme will have a limited cohort of 24 participants.

The relatively small cohort provides an opportunity for participants to engage closely with other professionals during the programme.

A limited cohort can also create an environment conducive to peer learning, discussion and professional networking.

Because only 24 places are available, applicants should make sure that their application clearly demonstrates their relevant professional experience and interest in innovation for sustainable development.

Programme Fees

The stated programme fee is:

USD $2,495

Applicants should take this cost into consideration when planning their participation.

However, the IDIA Academy has indicated that a limited number of fully subsidised IDIA scholarships are available.

These scholarships are specifically intended for individuals from the Global South.

Applicants who may face financial barriers should therefore carefully review the available funding information and determine whether they can be considered for a subsidised place.

Fully Subsidised IDIA Scholarships

One of the most important features of the 2026 programme is the availability of a limited number of fully subsidised scholarships.

These scholarships are intended for individuals from the Global South.

A fully subsidised scholarship can significantly reduce the financial barrier associated with the programme fee.

Because the number of scholarships is limited, applicants should not assume that applying automatically guarantees funding.

Candidates interested in financial support should carefully follow the application instructions and provide any information required to demonstrate their eligibility.

Application Period and Deadline

Applications for the IDIA Academy Managing Innovation for Impact Adaptive Leadership Programme 2026 opened on:

5 August 2026

The application window closes on:

28 August 2026

Application Deadline: 28 August 2026

Applicants should submit their applications before the deadline.

Given that the programme has only 24 available places, prospective participants should consider applying early rather than waiting until the final day.

How to Apply

Applicants interested in participating in the programme should complete the official application form provided by the IDIA Academy.

The application process requires candidates to submit the requested information through the programme’s application system.

Before applying, prospective participants should make sure that they understand:

  1. The programme objectives.
  2. The intended participant profile.
  3. The programme dates.
  4. The location in Ghana.
  5. The USD $2,495 programme fee.
  6. The availability of limited scholarships.
  7. The application deadline.
  8. The professional experience expected from participants.

Applicants should also ensure that the information provided in their application demonstrates how their professional work connects to innovation and sustainable development.

How to Make Your Application Stronger

Because this is a professional development programme targeting development innovation leaders, applicants should clearly demonstrate their connection to innovation and sustainable development.

1. Explain Your Professional Role

Clearly describe your current role and responsibilities.

If you manage programmes, innovation portfolios, funding initiatives, policy processes or scaling activities, explain your responsibilities and the impact of your work.

2. Demonstrate Your Innovation Experience

Do not simply state that you are interested in innovation.

Provide concrete examples of how you have:

  • Developed innovative approaches.
  • Managed innovation programmes.
  • Supported scaling.
  • Influenced innovation strategies.
  • Invested in innovative solutions.
  • Designed development interventions.
  • Worked with innovation ecosystems.

3. Connect Your Experience to Sustainable Development

Explain how your work contributes to addressing development challenges.

This could include work related to social development, health, climate, education, governance, technology, economic development or other areas.

4. Demonstrate Leadership

The programme focuses strongly on adaptive leadership.

Applicants should therefore demonstrate situations in which they have led teams, projects, organisational change, partnerships or innovation initiatives.

5. Show Your Interest in Learning

Explain how participation in the programme would strengthen your ability to manage innovation and create impact.

A strong application should demonstrate that you have both relevant experience and a clear reason for wanting to develop further.

APPLY HERE

Who Qualifies for the IDIA Academy Programme?

Professional Eligibility

The programme is designed for development practitioners, funders, decision-makers and innovation leaders who are driven to advance innovation for sustainable development.

It is particularly suited to professionals who:

  • Manage innovation portfolios.
  • Manage scaling programmes.
  • Influence country innovation ecosystem strategies.
  • Shape institutional innovation policy.
  • Invest in innovations addressing global development challenges.
  • Work within multilateral agencies.
  • Work within philanthropy.
  • Work within investment funds.
  • Work within civil society.
  • Have responsibilities connected to development innovation.

Geographic Eligibility

The programme information does not state that participation is restricted to a specific continent.

The programme is internationally oriented and targets professionals working in global development.

However, fully subsidised IDIA scholarships are specifically available to individuals from the Global South.

Applicants should therefore distinguish between general programme eligibility and scholarship eligibility.

African Applicants

Professionals from African countries can potentially apply, and Ghana is the host country for the 2026 programme.

African applicants who meet the professional profile and are interested in development innovation may be particularly relevant to the programme’s focus.

Global South Applicants

Individuals from the Global South are particularly important in relation to the available fully subsidised scholarships.

Applicants from developing-country contexts should therefore review the scholarship provisions carefully when completing their application.

Race and Ethnicity

The provided programme information does not specify a racial or ethnic restriction.

Eligibility is primarily described in terms of professional background, interest in development innovation and, for the subsidised scholarships, Global South eligibility.

Visit HERE to learn more about the IDIA Academy Adaptive Leadership Programme 2026 in Ghana.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the IDIA Academy Adaptive Leadership Programme 2026?

It is an intensive professional development programme designed to strengthen the leadership, innovation and systems-thinking capabilities of professionals working to advance sustainable development.

Where will the programme take place?

The 2026 programme will take place in Ghana.

When will the programme take place?

The programme is scheduled for 7–10 December 2026.

How many participants will be selected?

The programme has 24 places.

How much does the programme cost?

The stated fee is USD $2,495.

Are scholarships available?

Who should apply?

The programme is intended for development practitioners, funders, decision-makers and innovation leaders, particularly those managing innovation portfolios or scaling programmes, influencing innovation ecosystems, shaping institutional innovation policy or investing in innovations addressing global development challenges.

What is the application deadline?

The deadline is 28 August 2026.

Can professionals from Africa apply?

Conclusion

The IDIA Academy Managing Innovation for Impact Adaptive Leadership Programme 2026 presents an important professional development opportunity for people working at the intersection of innovation, international development, leadership and sustainable development.

The programme is particularly relevant to professionals who are responsible for managing innovation portfolios, scaling development solutions, influencing innovation ecosystems, shaping institutional policy or investing in innovations designed to address global challenges.

Participants will have the opportunity to strengthen their leadership capabilities, learn innovation and systems-thinking approaches, develop greater confidence in leading change and build relationships with a diverse international network of development professionals.

The availability of a limited number of fully subsidised scholarships for individuals from the Global South also makes the programme potentially accessible to professionals who may otherwise face financial barriers.

With only 24 places available, interested professionals should prepare their applications carefully and submit them before the 28 August 2026 deadline.

item.content:encoded:
Transparency International Defence & Security (TI-DS) is seeking an experienced and strategic Head of Policy to provide leadership on policy development, advocacy, stakeholder engagement and institutional reform within the global defence and security sector.

The position offers an opportunity for a senior policy professional with substantial experience in the defence and security space to influence policy at regional and global levels while contributing to efforts to create more transparent, accountable and corruption-free defence institutions.

The role is being recruited through Prospectus Recruitment Agency and is offered on a permanent contract, with a hybrid working arrangement combining work in London and remotely. The successful candidate should also be prepared for UK and international travel.

Opportunity Overview

Detail Information
Position Head of Policy
Organisation Transparency International Defence & Security (TI-DS)
Recruitment Agency Prospectus
Job Type Permanent
Work Arrangement Hybrid – London and remote
Salary Approximately £65,000 per year
Job Number 195498
Application Deadline 25 August 2026
Application Requirement CV only initially
Travel UK and international travel required
Sector Defence, security, policy, governance and anti-corruption

About Transparency International Defence & Security

Transparency International Defence & Security, commonly known as TI-DS, works to promote greater transparency, accountability and integrity within the defence and security sector.

The organisation is part of Transparency International, a global anti-corruption movement working to address corruption and strengthen accountability across societies and institutions.

TI-DS operates as a global centre of excellence focused specifically on the defence and security sector. Its work seeks to ensure that defence and security institutions operate in ways that serve citizens, states and the wider international community.

The organisation works to identify vulnerabilities, develop evidence-based policy approaches and support reforms that can strengthen governance and reduce opportunities for corruption and abuse.

TI-DS is hosted by the Transparency International chapter in the United Kingdom.

About the Head of Policy Position

The Head of Policy will occupy a senior leadership position within TI-DS and will be responsible for providing strategic direction to the organisation’s policy work.

The central purpose of the position is to help translate research, evidence and policy analysis into systemic change across defence and security institutions.

Rather than simply producing policy documents, the successful candidate will be expected to help ensure that TI-DS’s evidence informs decision-makers and contributes to meaningful institutional reforms.

The role therefore combines several areas of professional responsibility, including:

  • Strategic policy leadership
  • Policy development
  • Advocacy
  • Stakeholder engagement
  • International relations
  • Defence and security governance
  • Institutional reform
  • Evidence-based policy
  • Team management
  • Regional and global engagement
  • Influencing decision-makers

The successful candidate will become part of the TI-DS leadership team, contributing to the development and advancement of the organisation’s policy positions and broader strategic objectives.

Key Responsibilities

1. Provide Strategic Policy Leadership

One of the most important responsibilities of the Head of Policy will be providing strategic direction for TI-DS’s policy work.

The successful candidate will need to understand complex developments within defence and security and determine how evidence and research can be translated into practical policy recommendations.

This means identifying opportunities where TI-DS can influence discussions, reforms and decision-making processes at national, regional and international levels.

The postholder will contribute to ensuring that TI-DS’s policy positions are strategically aligned with its wider mission and available resources.

2. Translate Evidence Into Policy Impact

The position focuses heavily on connecting evidence with systemic change.

The successful applicant will be expected to help transform research and evidence into policy positions that can influence governments, institutions and other relevant stakeholders.

This requires the ability to:

  • Analyse complex policy issues.
  • Understand defence and security institutions.
  • Develop evidence-informed policy positions.
  • Identify opportunities for policy influence.
  • Communicate policy recommendations effectively.
  • Engage decision-makers.
  • Support reform processes.
  • Connect research findings with practical policy action.

Candidates should therefore be comfortable working at the intersection of research, policy and advocacy.

3. Lead Stakeholder Engagement

Stakeholder engagement will be a significant component of the role.

The Head of Policy will engage stakeholders at both regional and global levels, while also supporting nationally led efforts to influence decision-makers.

This requires strong interpersonal and relationship-building abilities.

Candidates should be capable of developing relationships with stakeholders across the defence and security sector and using professional networks to advance policy objectives.

Strong stakeholder engagement skills will be particularly important because the role requires the postholder to influence people and institutions operating in complex policy environments.

4. Influence Decision-Makers

The successful candidate will support efforts to encourage decision-makers to adopt reforms based on evidence-informed policy positions.

This requires more than technical policy knowledge. Candidates will need to demonstrate the ability to understand different stakeholder perspectives, build credibility and communicate compelling policy arguments.

The role is therefore particularly suited to professionals who have previously contributed to or successfully influenced policy development or policy reform.

5. Develop and Advance Policy Positions

As a member of the TI-DS leadership team, the Head of Policy will participate in formulating and advancing organisational policy positions.

This includes ensuring that policy work remains:

  • Evidence informed
  • Strategically relevant
  • Consistent with TI-DS’s mission
  • Capable of influencing decision-makers
  • Achievable within available budgets and resources

The postholder will need to balance ambitious policy objectives with organisational capacity and resource considerations.

6. Support Nationally Led Reform Efforts

Although TI-DS operates globally, the position will also support nationally led efforts to influence decision-makers and promote reforms.

This means the successful candidate should be comfortable working across different geographical and institutional contexts.

An understanding of how defence and security institutions operate in different countries will be valuable, as will experience working with diverse stakeholders.

7. Manage a Small Policy and Advocacy Team

The Head of Policy will also have management responsibilities.

The role involves managing a small team of advocacy and policy staff, meaning candidates should have some experience leading or managing teams.

The successful candidate will therefore need to demonstrate not only technical policy expertise but also the ability to:

  • Provide direction to colleagues.
  • Build effective working relationships.
  • Support staff development.
  • Coordinate policy and advocacy activities.
  • Manage priorities.
  • Encourage collaboration.
  • Contribute to a positive organisational culture.

While extensive management experience may not be the central requirement, some demonstrated experience of team management is expected.

Who Is the Ideal Candidate?

TI-DS is looking for an experienced professional with a substantial background in the defence and security sector.

The organisation specifically indicates that the successful candidate will bring significant experience from within the defence and security space.

This is therefore a particularly relevant opportunity for professionals whose careers have involved defence policy, security policy, governance, international security, defence institutions, security-sector reform or related areas.

Key Professional Experience

Strong candidates are expected to demonstrate:

  • Significant experience working in the defence and security space.
  • Experience developing or advancing policy.
  • A strong record of stakeholder engagement.
  • Established professional networks within the relevant sector.
  • Experience influencing policy or decision-making.
  • Some experience managing teams.
  • The ability to work strategically.
  • Strong communication and relationship-building skills.
  • Commitment to TI-DS’s mission.

Anti-Corruption Experience Is Not Essential

An important feature of this vacancy is that previous experience specifically in anti-corruption is not essential.

This makes the position potentially suitable for experienced defence and security professionals who may not have worked directly in the anti-corruption sector.

According to the vacancy information, knowledge of anti-corruption can be developed over time.

However, candidates should demonstrate empathy with and commitment to the mission of TI-DS and be willing to develop their understanding of anti-corruption issues as part of the role.

This distinction is important: applicants should not automatically exclude themselves simply because their professional background is primarily in defence or security rather than anti-corruption.

Stakeholder Engagement Skills

Strong stakeholder engagement is one of the central requirements of this position.

The successful candidate will be expected to leverage professional networks and relationships within the defence and security sector.

Candidates should therefore be able to demonstrate examples of working with senior stakeholders, institutions, policymakers, government representatives, civil society organisations, international organisations or other relevant actors.

Evidence of successfully building relationships and using those relationships to advance policy objectives can strengthen an application.

Policy Influence and Advocacy Experience

The vacancy places considerable emphasis on candidates having a demonstrable record of advancing policies.

Applicants should consider highlighting concrete examples where they have contributed to:

  • Policy development.
  • Policy reform.
  • Advocacy campaigns.
  • Government engagement.
  • Institutional change.
  • Strategic recommendations.
  • Defence or security policy.
  • International policy processes.
  • Stakeholder consultations.
  • Evidence-based decision-making.

Where possible, applicants should show the result or impact of their policy work rather than simply listing responsibilities.

For example, demonstrating that a policy recommendation contributed to a change in institutional practice can be more compelling than simply stating that the applicant participated in policy development.

Leadership and Team Management

The Head of Policy is a leadership-level position and includes responsibility for managing a small team.

Candidates should therefore be prepared to demonstrate previous experience working with or managing colleagues.

Relevant experience could include:

  • Managing policy teams.
  • Supervising advocacy staff.
  • Coordinating multidisciplinary teams.
  • Leading research or policy projects.
  • Mentoring junior colleagues.
  • Delegating responsibilities.
  • Managing competing priorities.
  • Delivering projects within available resources.

The role does not necessarily require an extensive history of senior management, but applicants should be able to demonstrate credible leadership experience.

Hybrid Working Arrangement

The position operates under a hybrid working model, combining work in London with remote working.

This provides flexibility compared with a fully office-based position, but applicants should note that this is not advertised as a completely location-independent global remote job.

The position is based around London and remote working, and the successful candidate will also be required to undertake UK and international travel.

Applicants outside the United Kingdom should therefore carefully consider the location requirements, travel expectations and any applicable right-to-work requirements before applying.

Salary and Employment Terms

The advertised salary is circa £65,000 per annum.

The position is offered on a permanent contract, making it a long-term employment opportunity rather than a temporary assignment, internship or short-term fellowship.

The combination of a permanent contract, senior-level responsibilities and hybrid working makes the vacancy potentially attractive to experienced professionals seeking a leadership position within the international defence, security and governance sector.

Application Process

Prospectus has stated that applicants should submit their CV only in the first instance.

Candidates may subsequently be asked to provide:

  • A supporting statement.
  • Additional information.
  • Further documentation as part of the recruitment process.

Applicants should therefore ensure that their CV clearly communicates their suitability for the position before submitting it.

What to Highlight in Your CV

Given the requirements of the position, applicants should consider clearly highlighting:

  1. Defence and security experience
    Explain the nature and level of your work within the sector.
  2. Policy experience
    Identify policies you have developed, influenced, implemented or advocated for.
  3. Stakeholder engagement
    Demonstrate your experience working with important stakeholders and decision-makers.
  4. Policy influence
    Include measurable examples of how your work contributed to policy or institutional change.
  5. Leadership experience
    Highlight teams, projects or programmes you have managed.
  6. International experience
    If applicable, demonstrate experience working across countries, regions or international institutions.
  7. Strategic thinking
    Show how you have contributed to organisational strategy or long-term policy objectives.
  8. Mission alignment
    Demonstrate your interest in transparency, accountability, integrity and improved governance within defence and security.

Application Deadline

The application deadline is 25 August 2026.

Applicants should submit their CV before the closing date and should avoid waiting until the final day to apply.

Because the recruitment agency may begin reviewing applications before the deadline, candidates should consider submitting a strong application as early as possible.

Who Can Apply?

Professional Category

This opportunity is primarily intended for experienced professionals in the defence and security sector, particularly individuals with substantial experience in policy, advocacy, stakeholder engagement or institutional reform.

It is not primarily an entry-level opportunity and is unlikely to be suitable for recent graduates without significant relevant professional experience.

Geographic Eligibility

The vacancy is advertised as a hybrid London and remote position, with UK and international travel required.

The provided vacancy information does not specify a nationality restriction, race or ethnicity requirement, or a list of eligible countries/continents.

Prospectus states that it welcomes applications from all sections of the community and is committed to building inclusive and diverse organisations.

However, because the position has a London-based hybrid arrangement and involves international travel, applicants outside the United Kingdom should verify the applicable employment, location and right-to-work requirements during the recruitment process.

Racial and Ethnic Eligibility

There is no race or ethnicity restriction stated in the vacancy information.

The recruitment agency explicitly indicates that applications are welcomed from all sections of the community.

Qualifications and Experience

The most important eligibility factor is professional experience rather than a particular nationality or racial background.

The strongest candidates are expected to have:

  • Significant experience in defence and security.
  • Demonstrable policy experience.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Relevant professional networks.
  • A record of advancing policies.
  • Some team management experience.
  • A commitment to the TI-DS mission.

Previous anti-corruption experience is not mandatory, as the vacancy indicates that this knowledge can be developed.

Why This Opportunity Is Significant

The Head of Policy role provides an opportunity to work on issues that affect the governance and accountability of defence and security institutions around the world.

Defence and security institutions control substantial public resources and operate in areas that can have significant consequences for citizens and states. Strengthening transparency and accountability within these institutions can therefore contribute to better governance and more effective use of public resources.

For an experienced policy professional, the role offers the opportunity to combine policy leadership, advocacy, stakeholder engagement and international work in a mission-driven organisation.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Before submitting your CV, review your professional experience against the requirements of the vacancy.

A strong application should make it easy for the recruiter to identify evidence of your suitability.

Recommended CV Structure

Consider organising your CV around:

Professional Profile:
Provide a concise summary demonstrating your senior-level experience in defence, security, policy or a closely related field.

Core Competencies:
Include relevant areas such as policy development, advocacy, stakeholder engagement, strategic leadership, defence and security, governance and team management.

Professional Experience:
Focus on achievements rather than simply listing duties.

Policy and Advocacy Achievements:
Where appropriate, identify specific policies, reforms or initiatives you helped advance.

Leadership Experience:
Clearly demonstrate experience managing teams, projects or strategic initiatives.

International Experience:
Include international, regional or cross-border work where relevant.

Use Evidence and Results

Instead of simply writing:

Responsible for stakeholder engagement.

A stronger CV could explain the nature and outcome of the engagement, such as:

Developed and maintained relationships with senior institutional stakeholders, supporting evidence-based policy recommendations and contributing to the adoption of governance reforms.

The objective is to demonstrate impact, influence and leadership.

APPLY HERE

About Prospectus

Prospectus is the recruitment agency managing the recruitment process for this vacancy.

The agency states that it is committed to supporting candidates throughout their recruitment journey and to helping organisations build inclusive and diverse teams.

Applicants should follow the recruitment instructions provided for Job #195498 when submitting their application.

Visit HERE to learn more abou the Head of Policy at Transparency International Defence & Security

Conclusion

The Head of Policy at Transparency International Defence & Security is a senior-level opportunity for an experienced defence and security professional who wants to use policy, advocacy and stakeholder engagement to contribute to greater transparency and accountability in the global defence sector.

The successful candidate will play an important role in translating evidence into policy impact, influencing decision-makers, strengthening stakeholder relationships and supporting nationally led reform efforts. The position also provides an opportunity to join the TI-DS leadership team and manage a small policy and advocacy team.

With a circa £65,000 annual salary, permanent employment, a hybrid London and remote working arrangement, and opportunities for UK and international travel, the position could be particularly relevant to established professionals seeking to take their defence and security policy career into a strategic leadership role.

Deadline: 25 August 2026.
