item.content:encoded:
The Disability Inclusion Partnerships 2026 programme is now open, offering grants of up to £25,000 to support international partnerships that strengthen disability inclusion in higher education. The initiative brings together eligible higher education institutions in the United Kingdom and partner institutions from 10 participating countries to identify barriers faced by persons with disabilities and develop practical, sustainable solutions.

The programme is designed to promote more inclusive higher education systems by supporting institutional collaboration, policy development, evidence generation, knowledge exchange, and the participation of persons with disabilities in decision-making.

For institutions working to make higher education more accessible, equitable, and disability-inclusive, this funding provides an opportunity to collaborate internationally and implement meaningful institutional change.

Disability Inclusion Partnerships 2026 at a Glance

  • Programme: Disability Inclusion Partnerships 2026
  • Funding: Up to £25,000 per partnership
  • Project duration: 17 months
  • Expected project start: 1 January 2027
  • Publication date: 20 July 2026
  • Clarification deadline: 11 September 2026
  • Application deadline: 21 September 2026
  • Submission time: 11:00 a.m. BST
  • Application platform: Good Grants
  • Lead applicant: Eligible UK higher education institution
  • International partners: Institutions in one of 10 participating countries
  • Partnership requirement: UK higher education institution + eligible partner institution in a participating country

What Is the Disability Inclusion Partnerships 2026 Programme?

Disability Inclusion Partnerships 2026 provides funding for partnerships between higher education institutions in the UK and institutions in selected international partner countries.

The programme focuses on addressing barriers that prevent persons with disabilities from fully participating, progressing, and succeeding in higher education.

Rather than focusing only on individual support, the grants encourage institutions to examine their broader systems, policies, practices, learning environments, governance structures, and decision-making processes.

Through international collaboration and knowledge exchange, participating institutions are expected to identify challenges and develop approaches that can produce lasting institutional improvements.

The programme therefore places considerable emphasis on sustainable institutional change, rather than short-term interventions.

Which Countries Can Participate?

For the 2026 funding round, eligible UK institutions can establish partnerships with institutions in the following 10 countries:

  1. Bangladesh
  2. Ghana
  3. Indonesia
  4. Kenya
  5. Malaysia
  6. Nigeria
  7. South Africa
  8. Sri Lanka
  9. Ukraine
  10. Uzbekistan

This makes the opportunity particularly relevant to higher education institutions in Africa, Asia, and Europe that are interested in collaborating with UK institutions on disability inclusion.

However, institutions should carefully review the official Call Guidance because country-specific eligibility requirements and priorities may apply.

Objectives of the Disability Inclusion Partnerships Grants

The programme has several interconnected objectives aimed at strengthening disability inclusion across higher education.

1. Strengthen Disability-Inclusive Policies and Systems

One of the central objectives is to help higher education institutions develop or strengthen policies, systems, and institutional practices that promote disability inclusion.

Projects could therefore examine how existing institutional policies address disability and identify areas where improvements are required.

This may include reviewing institutional approaches to accessibility, teaching and learning, student services, research, governance, recruitment, staff support, and participation.

2. Improve Participation and Outcomes for Persons with Disabilities

The programme seeks to improve opportunities for persons with disabilities to access and participate successfully in higher education.

This extends beyond admission and includes the ability of students and staff with disabilities to participate fully in institutional life and achieve positive outcomes.

Projects should therefore consider the barriers that may affect participation, progression, retention, achievement, and success.

3. Promote Sustainable Institutional Change

The grants are intended to support changes that can continue beyond the lifetime of the funded project.

Partnerships are encouraged to generate evidence, strengthen institutional capacity, develop sustainable approaches, and share knowledge that can influence long-term disability-inclusive practice.

Expected Outcomes of Funded Projects

Successful projects are expected to contribute to one or more of several outcomes.

Stronger Institutional Leadership and Governance

Projects may help institutions strengthen leadership, governance, and organisational capacity to implement disability-inclusive policies and practices.

This could involve improving institutional structures, responsibilities, accountability mechanisms, or leadership approaches related to disability inclusion.

More Accessible Learning, Teaching and Research Environments

Another expected outcome is the creation of more accessible and inclusive environments for students and staff with disabilities.

Projects may address barriers within teaching, learning, research, institutional facilities, services, or other aspects of the higher education experience.

The goal is to ensure that disability inclusion becomes part of institutional practice rather than being treated as an isolated issue.

Better Evidence on Disability Inclusion

Projects can also contribute to improved understanding of the barriers and enabling factors affecting persons with disabilities in higher education.

Generating reliable evidence can help institutions understand where challenges exist and determine which approaches can produce meaningful improvements.

Implementation of Inclusive Policies and Frameworks

The programme also encourages institutions to move from policy development to implementation.

Successful projects may support the development, improvement, or implementation of policies and frameworks that embed disability-inclusive practices within institutional systems.

Stronger External Partnerships

Projects are expected, where appropriate, to strengthen relationships between higher education institutions and external stakeholders.

These may include:

  • Organisations of disabled people
  • Employers
  • Civil society organisations
  • Other relevant external stakeholders

Such relationships can help institutions improve participation and progression not only during higher education but also as students and graduates transition into employment and wider society.

Greater Voice and Agency for Disabled People

An important element of the programme is increasing the involvement of disabled people in institutional decision-making.

Projects can contribute to greater participation, voice, and agency for disabled people in shaping:

  • Institutional policies
  • Academic practices
  • Support systems
  • Decision-making processes
  • Disability inclusion strategies

This approach recognises persons with disabilities as active contributors to institutional change rather than simply recipients of support.

Greater Integration of Intersectional Approaches

The programme also encourages institutions to consider intersectionality when developing policies and practices.

This means recognising that disability can intersect with other factors and circumstances that may influence a person’s experience within higher education.

Institutions are therefore encouraged to consider how different experiences and forms of disadvantage may interact when developing inclusive approaches.

Who Is Eligible to Apply?

The Disability Inclusion Partnerships 2026 grants are institutional partnership grants, rather than individual scholarships or grants for individual applicants.

A partnership must include:

  • One eligible UK higher education institution, and
  • One partner institution in one of the 10 participating countries.

The partnership must satisfy the eligibility requirements specified in the official Call Guidance.

UK Institution Eligibility

The UK lead institution must be a higher education provider with degree-awarding powers.

The UK institution serves as the lead applicant and is responsible for submitting the application through the designated online grant platform.

Overseas Institution Eligibility

The overseas partner must meet the eligibility requirements specified in the Call Guidance for the relevant participating country.

Because requirements may differ between participating countries, institutions should not assume that every higher education institution automatically qualifies.

Applicants should therefore consult the country-specific sections of the official guidance before developing and submitting their application.

How the Partnership Application Works

Applications must be jointly developed by the UK and overseas lead institutions.

This means the proposal should be developed collaboratively rather than being prepared independently by one institution.

The partnership should demonstrate a clear understanding of the disability inclusion challenge being addressed and explain how the proposed collaboration will contribute to meaningful institutional change.

The completed application must be submitted by the UK lead institution.

Importantly, online applications can only be started and submitted by the lead UK institution.

Grant Amount and Project Duration

Successful partnerships can receive a grant of up to £25,000.

Funded projects will have a duration of 17 months, with projects scheduled to begin on:

1 January 2027

The 17-month timeframe provides participating institutions with an opportunity to develop their partnership, investigate disability inclusion challenges, implement activities, generate evidence, exchange knowledge, and work towards sustainable institutional change.

Applicants should therefore ensure that proposed activities are realistic and achievable within the project period.

Application Deadline

The final submission deadline for Disability Inclusion Partnerships 2026 is:

21 September 2026 at 11:00 a.m. BST

Applicants should not wait until the final day to submit their application. Because the programme requires collaboration between UK and international institutions, partnerships should allow sufficient time for planning, drafting, reviewing, institutional approval, and submission.

Important Clarification Deadline

The deadline for submitting clarification questions is:

11 September 2026

Questions relating to the programme should be sent to: goingglobalpartnerships-DIP@britishcouncil.org

Institutions with questions about eligibility, country-specific requirements, application procedures, or other aspects of the call should seek clarification before the clarification deadline.

How to Apply for Disability Inclusion Partnerships 2026

Applications must be submitted through the programme’s online grant platform.

The application process can be approached through the following steps.

Step 1: Identify an Eligible Partner

Eligible UK institutions should identify a suitable partner institution in one of the 10 participating countries.

Similarly, institutions in the participating countries should seek collaboration with an eligible UK higher education institution.

The partnership should have a clear shared interest in disability inclusion and the capacity to deliver the proposed project.

Step 2: Review the Call Guidance

Before developing the proposal, both institutions should carefully review the official Disability Inclusion Partnerships 2026: Call Guidance.

The guidance contains important information concerning:

  • Eligibility
  • Country-specific requirements
  • Programme priorities
  • Application requirements
  • Project expectations
  • Funding conditions
  • Other requirements that applicants need to satisfy

This step is particularly important because eligibility requirements may differ across participating countries.

Step 3: Develop the Project Jointly

The UK and overseas institutions should jointly develop the proposal.

The project should clearly identify the disability inclusion challenge, explain why it matters, and demonstrate how the partnership will address the issue.

A strong proposal should establish a logical connection between:

Problem → Partnership → Activities → Evidence → Institutional Change → Sustainable Outcomes

Step 4: Prepare the Application

Applicants should complete the required online application and prepare any supporting information requested in the Call Guidance.

An offline sample of the application form is available to help institutions understand the information required before completing the online submission.

Step 5: Register on the Grant Platform

Applications must be submitted through the online grant platform, and registration is required.

The designated platform is the Going Global Partnerships grant platform.

The application should be made using the form:

“Going Global Partnerships – Multi-country – Disability Inclusion Partnerships 2026.”

Step 6: Submit Through the UK Lead Institution

The final application must be submitted by the eligible UK lead institution.

Online applications can only be started and submitted by the lead UK institution.

Partnerships should therefore ensure that the UK lead institution has sufficient time to complete the online process before the deadline.

What Should Applicants Consider When Developing a Strong Proposal?

Although applicants should follow the official Call Guidance for the complete requirements, partnerships can strengthen their preparation by considering several key areas.

Clearly Define the Disability Inclusion Problem

A proposal should clearly explain the specific challenge affecting persons with disabilities within the participating institutions.

Rather than describing disability inclusion generally, the partnership should demonstrate an understanding of the particular barriers it intends to address.

Demonstrate the Need for the Partnership

The proposal should explain why collaboration between the UK institution and international partner is valuable.

Applicants should demonstrate how international knowledge exchange, comparative experience, expertise, or collaborative learning can contribute to the proposed institutional change.

Focus on Institutional Change

The programme is intended to strengthen institutional systems, policies, practices, and capacity.

Projects should therefore demonstrate how their activities can contribute to changes that extend beyond individual beneficiaries or short-term interventions.

Include Persons with Disabilities in the Process

Given the programme’s emphasis on voice and agency, applicants should consider meaningful ways of involving disabled people in the design, implementation, evaluation, and decision-making processes of the project.

Consider Sustainability

A strong project should explain what happens after the 17-month funding period.

Applicants should consider how successful policies, practices, evidence, partnerships, or institutional mechanisms can continue after the grant ends.

Consider External Stakeholders

Where appropriate, institutions should consider how collaboration with organisations of disabled people, employers, civil society, and other stakeholders could strengthen project outcomes.

This can help connect disability inclusion within higher education to broader participation, employment, and social outcomes.

Application Documents

Applicants should consult the programme materials provided for the 2026 call.

The available documents include:

  1. Disability Inclusion Partnerships 2026: Call Guidance
  2. Disability Inclusion Partnerships 2026: Reference Application Form — provided for reference and not for submission
  3. Disability Inclusion Partnerships 2026: Sample Grant Agreement

These documents should be reviewed carefully before an application is prepared.

APPLY HERE

Why This Opportunity Matters

Disability inclusion in higher education requires more than providing individual accommodations. Institutions may need to examine policies, infrastructure, teaching and learning practices, research environments, governance, student services, staff support, and institutional culture.

The Disability Inclusion Partnerships programme provides a framework for institutions to address these issues collaboratively.

The international nature of the programme also creates opportunities for higher education institutions to learn from different approaches to accessibility and inclusion.

For participating institutions, the potential value extends beyond the grant itself. Partnerships can contribute to:

  • Institutional capacity building
  • Policy improvement
  • International knowledge exchange
  • Evidence generation
  • Accessibility improvements
  • Stronger stakeholder engagement
  • Greater participation of persons with disabilities
  • More inclusive institutional decision-making
  • Long-term organisational change

Visit HERE to learn more about the Disability Inclusion Partnerships 2026.

Important Information for Kenyan Institutions

Kenya is one of the 10 countries eligible to participate in the 2026 programme.

Kenyan higher education institutions that meet the applicable eligibility requirements can therefore explore partnerships with eligible UK higher education institutions.

However, Kenyan institutions should review the country-specific requirements in the Call Guidance before assuming eligibility.

A potential Kenyan-UK partnership should also ensure that the proposed project addresses a clearly defined disability inclusion challenge within higher education and demonstrates how collaboration can produce sustainable institutional improvements.

Key Dates to Remember

  • 20 July 2026: Programme publication date

item.content:encoded:
The Heinrich Böll Stiftung’s Global Unit for Democracy and Human Rights in Brussels is inviting applications for its Traineeship Programme 2026, offering an early-career opportunity for qualified graduates interested in democracy, human rights, international affairs, civil society, research, communications, and social justice.

The traineeship will take place in Brussels, Belgium, from 15 September 2026 to 31 December 2026. The programme is designed to provide practical professional experience while allowing the successful trainee to contribute to the ongoing work of the Global Unit for Democracy and Human Rights.

The application deadline is Sunday, 16 August 2026 at 23:59 CEST.

This opportunity may be particularly valuable for recent Master’s graduates who want to gain practical experience in an international, multicultural environment and develop their skills in project support, research, administration, communications, event organization, and stakeholder engagement.

About the Heinrich Böll Stiftung Global Unit for Democracy and Human Rights

The Global Unit for Democracy and Human Rights is an important part of the Heinrich Böll Stiftung’s international work.

The Unit focuses on strengthening democratic societies, advancing human rights, supporting civic participation, and promoting international solidarity.

Its key areas of work include:

  • Strengthening democratic institutions and civil society around the world
  • Advancing human rights
  • Promoting gender democracy
  • Supporting LGBTIQ+ rights
  • Protecting minority rights
  • Countering authoritarianism
  • Promoting civic participation
  • Supporting human rights defenders
  • Supporting political activists working in restrictive environments
  • Building transnational networks
  • Promoting global solidarity and advocacy

The traineeship therefore provides exposure to a range of international policy, human rights, democracy, advocacy, research, communications, and organizational activities.

Purpose of the Traineeship

The main purpose of the traineeship is twofold.

First, the trainee will provide practical support to the work of the Global Unit for Democracy and Human Rights.

Second, the programme is intended to provide the trainee with meaningful learning opportunities and hands-on professional experience.

The successful candidate will have the opportunity to gain insight into:

  • Project implementation
  • Project monitoring
  • Administration
  • Organizational management
  • Research and analysis
  • Communications
  • Event coordination
  • Stakeholder engagement
  • International human rights and democracy work

Because the position covers multiple areas, it can provide an excellent foundation for someone beginning a career in international development, human rights, public policy, political science, communications, civil society, or related fields.

Key Responsibilities

The selected trainee will contribute to different work streams within the Global Unit.

1. Administrative and Operational Support

The trainee will assist with day-to-day administrative and organizational responsibilities.

Tasks may include:

  • Supporting routine administrative activities
  • Assisting with organizational tasks
  • Supporting administration and logistics
  • Helping prepare reports
  • Preparing meeting materials
  • Providing general operational assistance to the Unit

This part of the role requires strong organization, attention to detail, reliability, and the ability to manage multiple tasks.

2. Project Support

The trainee will also contribute to the implementation and monitoring of projects.

Responsibilities may include:

  • Supporting project implementation
  • Assisting with project monitoring
  • Preparing project documentation
  • Organizing relevant project information
  • Supporting coordination with internal stakeholders
  • Supporting communication with external stakeholders

This experience can help candidates understand how international projects are planned, implemented, monitored, and documented.

3. Research and Analysis

Research is another important component of the traineeship.

The trainee may be expected to:

  • Conduct background research
  • Research topics relevant to the Unit’s work
  • Collect information from different sources
  • Analyze information
  • Summarize research findings
  • Prepare briefing notes
  • Prepare concise summaries
  • Produce other research-related outputs

Candidates with strong analytical, research, writing, and information-management skills will therefore be well positioned for the role.

4. Events and Outreach

The trainee will support the organization of events and other activities.

This may include assisting with:

  • Workshops
  • Meetings
  • Conferences
  • Public events
  • Participant management
  • Event logistics
  • Follow-up activities
  • Meeting minutes
  • Summary notes

The trainee may also attend relevant meetings and help document key discussions and outcomes.

This provides practical exposure to event coordination and stakeholder engagement in an international environment.

5. Communications

The role also involves communications support.

The trainee may assist with:

  • Preparing website content
  • Preparing newsletter content
  • Supporting other communication channels
  • Disseminating information
  • Communicating project results
  • Preparing materials for external audiences

This makes communication skills particularly important for applicants.

Essential Qualifications

Applicants must meet the core requirements established for the traineeship.

Master’s Degree

Candidates should hold a Master’s degree in a relevant field, such as:

  • Political Science
  • Economics
  • International Relations
  • Communications
  • Law
  • Social Sciences
  • Other related disciplines

Applicants who are expecting to graduate may provide proof of expected graduation.

Early-Career Profile

The traineeship is specifically intended as an early-career opportunity.

Preference will therefore be given to candidates with limited professional experience, including limited internship experience.

This means the programme is particularly suitable for recent graduates who are looking to gain their first substantial professional experience in the field.

Candidates should not be discouraged if they do not have many years of professional experience, as the position is deliberately designed to support early-career development.

Organizational and Administrative Skills

Candidates should demonstrate:

  • Strong organizational abilities
  • Good administrative skills
  • Excellent attention to detail
  • Ability to manage tasks effectively
  • Ability to work systematically

These skills are important because the trainee will contribute to administrative, project, event, and operational activities.

Communication Skills

Applicants must have excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.

Strong communication skills will be important for:

  • Writing reports
  • Preparing summaries
  • Drafting communication materials
  • Participating in meetings
  • Supporting events
  • Communicating with colleagues and stakeholders

Microsoft Office Skills

Candidates should be proficient in Microsoft Office applications, including:

  • Microsoft Word
  • Microsoft Excel
  • Microsoft PowerPoint
  • Microsoft Outlook

These tools may be used for administrative work, presentations, documentation, communication, and project support.

Interpersonal and Teamwork Skills

Applicants should have strong interpersonal skills and be able to work effectively in a:

  • Multicultural environment
  • Collaborative environment
  • International organization

The ability to work with people from different backgrounds is particularly important given the international nature of the Heinrich Böll Stiftung’s work.

Interest in Democracy and Human Rights

Applicants should demonstrate a genuine interest in the foundation’s:

  • Mission
  • Values
  • Areas of work

A strong interest in democracy and human rights should also be reflected in the applicant’s motivation letter.

Desirable Qualifications

In addition to the essential requirements, some additional experience may strengthen an application.

Desirable qualifications include:

  • Previous internship experience
  • Volunteer experience
  • Relevant extracurricular activities
  • Knowledge of German
  • Knowledge of French
  • Knowledge of Dutch
  • Experience supporting projects
  • Event organization experience
  • Communications experience
  • Research experience
  • Stakeholder engagement experience

These qualifications are described as desirable rather than essential.

Applicants who meet the core requirements but do not possess every desirable qualification may still be considered.

Eligibility Requirements

One of the most important aspects of this opportunity is the work-eligibility requirement.

Applicants must:

  • Be eligible to work in Belgium
  • Be available for a full-time traineeship in Brussels
  • Be able to participate under the Convention d’Immersion Professionnelle (CIP)
  • Have the appropriate Belgian work/residence authorization or qualifying EU/EEA citizenship

The organization states that it cannot provide visa sponsorship.

Therefore, applicants who would require the organization to sponsor a Belgian work visa or residence permit should carefully consider this requirement before applying.

Who Can Apply From Outside Belgium?

The opportunity welcomes candidates from diverse backgrounds, but the work authorization requirement is important.

The information provided specifically states that applicants must either have:

  • A valid work/residence permit for Belgium, or
  • EU/EEA citizenship

Applicants from outside the EU/EEA who do not already have the required Belgian work/residence authorization may therefore not be eligible, because visa sponsorship is not provided.

Consequently, this should not be presented as an opportunity open to applicants from every country.

Diversity and Inclusion

The Heinrich Böll Stiftung states that it welcomes applications from all backgrounds.

The organization is committed to:

  • Gender democracy
  • Anti-discrimination
  • Diversity
  • Inclusion

The opportunity does not specify a racial or ethnic restriction.

However, the requirement to be legally eligible to work in Belgium remains applicable regardless of an applicant’s background.

Traineeship Duration and Dates

The programme is scheduled to run for approximately three and a half months.

Start Date

15 September 2026

End Date

31 December 2026

Working Hours

Full-time, 37 hours per week

Location

Brussels, Belgium

Hybrid working arrangements may be discussed, although applicants should be prepared for the full-time nature of the traineeship and the requirement to be eligible to work in Belgium.

Application Deadline

Sunday, 16 August 2026 at 23:59 CEST

This is the final deadline for applications.

Applicants should not wait until the final hours to submit their materials because incomplete or late applications may not be considered.

Required Application Documents

Applicants must submit a complete application containing the required documents.

1. Curriculum Vitae

Applicants must provide a:

CV of no more than one page

The CV should clearly present the applicant’s:

  • Educational background
  • Relevant experience
  • Skills
  • Internships
  • Volunteer activities
  • Research experience
  • Extracurricular activities
  • Other relevant achievements

Because the CV is limited to one page, candidates should prioritize information that directly relates to the traineeship.

2. Motivation Letter

Applicants must submit a:

Motivation letter of no more than one page

The letter should address:

  • Relevant experience
  • Relevant skills
  • Interest in democracy and human rights work

Applicants should use the motivation letter to explain why they are interested in the traineeship and how their academic and practical background relates to the work of the Global Unit for Democracy and Human Rights.

A clear and specific motivation letter can help demonstrate genuine interest in the organization’s mission.

3. Master’s Degree Certificate

Applicants must provide:

  • A copy of their Master’s diploma, or
  • Proof of expected graduation

Candidates should ensure that the document clearly demonstrates their academic qualification or expected completion.

How to Submit the Application

Applications should be submitted by email.

Email Address

eui-info@eu.boell.org

Required Subject Line

“Trainee – Global Unit Democracy & Human Rights”

Applicants should use the specified subject line to ensure that their application can be properly identified and processed.

Interview Process

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Interviews are expected to take place in:

Late August 2026

The interview may be conducted:

  • Online, or
  • In person

Applicants should therefore remain available during this period after submitting their application.

What Candidates Can Gain From the Experience

Although this traineeship is not described as a scholarship or fellowship, it offers valuable professional development for candidates beginning careers in international and public-interest fields.

Through the position, a trainee can gain practical exposure to:

  • Democracy and human rights work
  • International organizations
  • Project management
  • Research and analysis
  • Policy-related work
  • Communications
  • Event management
  • Stakeholder coordination
  • Administration
  • Multicultural teamwork
  • International advocacy

The broad range of responsibilities can help an early-career professional develop transferable skills that may be useful in future roles within government, civil society, international organizations, research institutions, advocacy organizations, communications, and related sectors.

Important Considerations Before Applying

Applicants should carefully consider the following before submitting an application:

Work Authorization

The organization does not provide visa sponsorship.

Applicants must already have the appropriate authorization to work in Belgium or qualify through EU/EEA citizenship.

Full-Time Commitment

The traineeship requires 37 hours per week.

Candidates should ensure that they are available for the entire period from September through December 2026.

Brussels Location

The position is based in Brussels, Belgium.

Early-Career Focus

The traineeship is designed for early-career candidates, with preference given to applicants with limited professional experience.

One-Page Documents

The CV and motivation letter each have a strict maximum length of one page.

Applicants should therefore make their documents focused and relevant.

Application Timeline

Stage Date
Application deadline 16 August 2026, 23:59 CEST
Interviews Late August 2026
Traineeship begins 15 September 2026
Traineeship ends 31 December 2026

                                          Read More  HERE

Application Checklist

Before submitting, applicants should confirm that they have:

  • A relevant Master’s degree or proof of expected graduation
  • A one-page CV
  • A one-page motivation letter
  • Demonstrated interest in democracy and human rights
  • Relevant academic or practical experience
  • Strong English communication skills
  • Microsoft Office proficiency
  • Strong organizational and interpersonal skills
  • Eligibility to work in Belgium
  • Availability for a full-time traineeship
  • Appropriate Belgian work/residence authorization or EU/EEA citizenship
  • Used the correct email address
  • Used the required email subject line
  • Submitted the application before 16 August 2026 at 23:59 CEST

Conclusion

The Heinrich Böll Stiftung Global Unit for Democracy and Human Rights Traineeship Programme 2026 is a valuable early-career opportunity for Master’s graduates interested in democracy, human rights, international relations, public policy, communications, research, and civil society.

The traineeship provides practical experience across administration, project support, research and analysis, events, outreach, communications, and stakeholder engagement while exposing the successful candidate to the work of an international organization in Brussels.

Candidates should pay particular attention to the eligibility requirements. The organization does not provide visa sponsorship, and applicants must already be eligible to work in Belgium. The programme is full-time, runs from 15 September to 31 December 2026, and requires 37 hours per week.

Interested candidates should prepare a focused one-page CV, a strong one-page motivation letter, and proof of their Master’s qualification or expected graduation. Applications must be submitted by email by Sunday, 16 August 2026 at 23:59 CEST.

For early-career professionals who meet the work-authorization requirements and have a genuine interest in democracy and human rights, this traineeship can provide valuable practical experience and an opportunity to contribute to meaningful international work.

item.content:encoded:
The University of Notre Dame Provost’s Postdoctoral Fellowship Program 2027–2029 is inviting applications from outstanding early-career scholars seeking to advance their academic careers in an intellectually rigorous environment that combines disciplinary expertise with interdisciplinary collaboration.

The fellowship is offered through the College of Arts & Letters at the University of Notre Dame in Notre Dame, Indiana, United States. For the 2027–2029 academic years, the College will appoint a cohort of eight postdoctoral fellows, with one fellow hosted by each of eight participating departments, institutes, or programs.

Selected fellows will receive an annual salary of $75,000 together with an additional $15,000 per year for research-related expenses and further professional training. Fellows will also receive faculty mentorship, office space, professional development opportunities, and opportunities to participate in university-wide academic activities.

The application deadline is December 1, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time, and decisions are expected by March 1, 2027.

This opportunity is particularly suited to exceptional early-career researchers who want to strengthen their research, publishing, grant-writing, teaching, interdisciplinary collaboration, and academic leadership skills.

About the University of Notre Dame Provost’s Postdoctoral Fellowship Program

The Provost’s Postdoctoral Fellowship Program was developed to support outstanding early-career scholars who are interested in producing high-quality research while making meaningful contributions to society.

The programme is designed around several major objectives.

These include:

  • Supporting exceptional early-career scholars
  • Providing rigorous disciplinary mentorship
  • Encouraging interdisciplinary conversation and collaboration
  • Strengthening the scholarly reputation of participating departments and institutes
  • Promoting research connected to University Strategic Framework initiatives
  • Developing fellows’ research skills
  • Supporting academic publishing
  • Strengthening grant-writing abilities
  • Developing teaching skills
  • Providing professional development opportunities
  • Creating opportunities for academic networking and collaboration

The programme therefore goes beyond simply providing a postdoctoral position. It is structured as a two-year postdoctoral training and professional development experience intended to help fellows establish themselves as independent scholars and advance toward future academic careers.

For the 2027–2029 academic years, the College of Arts & Letters plans to appoint eight postdoctoral fellows in residence at the University of Notre Dame.

Each of the following units will host one fellow:

  1. Department of Art, Art History, and Design
  2. Department of English
  3. Department of German, Slavic, and Eurasian Studies
  4. Department of Philosophy
  5. Department of Romance Languages and Literatures
  6. Department of Theology
  7. Initiative on Race and Resilience
  8. Program in History and Philosophy of Science

Applicants are encouraged to explore the research interests and opportunities within these hosting units and identify an area in which their proposed research can make a strong scholarly contribution.

Fellowship Duration

The Provost’s Postdoctoral Fellowship is a two-year appointment.

The fellowship covers the 2027–2029 academic years, with fellows expected to be in residence at the University of Notre Dame.

The programme is designed to provide sufficient time for fellows to develop their research agendas, produce scholarly publications, pursue additional training, participate in academic activities, and build professional networks.

Fellowship Salary and Financial Support

One of the major attractions of the University of Notre Dame Provost’s Postdoctoral Fellowship is its financial support.

Selected fellows will receive:

Annual Salary: $75,000

Each fellow will receive an annual salary of:

$75,000

Additional Research and Training Support: $15,000 Per Year

Fellows will also receive:

$15,000 annually

to support expenses related to:

  • Research
  • Professional training
  • Scholarly activities
  • Other approved research-related needs

Over the two-year fellowship, the stated salary amounts represent:

  • $150,000 in salary over two years
  • Up to $30,000 in additional research and training support over two years

This provides substantial financial support for early-career scholars as they develop their academic careers.

Faculty Mentorship

Mentorship is an important component of the fellowship.

Hosting units will provide fellows with office space and work with the Director of Postdoctoral Studies in the College to identify appropriate primary faculty mentors for fellows’ proposed research projects.

Applicants may identify faculty members whose expertise aligns with their proposed research and explain why they would benefit from their mentorship.

Co-mentors with appointments at the University may also be identified at the discretion of the Director and the relevant hosting units.

An important instruction for applicants is that they should not contact faculty in the hosting department or institute to arrange a primary mentor or co-mentor before submitting the application.

Applicants can instead identify potential mentors within their research statement and explain why their expertise would be relevant to the proposed project.

Research and Professional Development

The fellowship is intended to help scholars develop the skills required for a successful academic career.

Fellows will have opportunities to strengthen their abilities in:

  • Research
  • Academic publishing
  • Grant writing
  • Teaching
  • Interdisciplinary collaboration
  • Professional networking
  • Academic communication
  • Research presentation
  • Career development

The fellows will also participate in a university-wide cohort of distinguished researchers.

This cohort will regularly participate in:

  • Lectures
  • Colloquia
  • Panel discussions
  • Academic networking
  • Research-related activities

These activities are intended to advance the fellows’ research and professional career aspirations.

Interdisciplinary Research Opportunities at Notre Dame

The University of Notre Dame has established strategic initiatives intended to identify areas where the University can make significant contributions to major global and societal challenges.

The University has identified areas including:

  • Arts
  • Data, artificial intelligence, and computing
  • Democracy
  • Ethics
  • Health and well-being
  • Sustainability
  • Global Catholicism

The University also maintains research strengths in traditional academic disciplines and operates more than 30 university-wide interdisciplinary centers and institutes.

Applicants are encouraged to explore these opportunities when developing their research proposals.

A strong application should demonstrate how the applicant’s research fits within the relevant academic environment and, where appropriate, how it could contribute to interdisciplinary research or broader University priorities.

Who Can Apply?

The fellowship is designed for outstanding early-career scholars.

Applicants must have successfully completed, or plan to complete, a doctoral degree within the specified eligibility period.

Specifically, applicants must have completed or plan to complete their doctoral degree between:

June 2024 and June 2027

Earlier doctoral completion dates may be considered where the applicant had qualifying:

  • Maternity leave
  • Paternity leave
  • Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) leave

within the previous two years.

Nationality Eligibility

The University states that:

Scholars of all nationalities may apply.

Therefore, the fellowship is open to qualified applicants regardless of country of citizenship or nationality.

There is no stated restriction limiting applications to applicants from the United States, North America, Europe, Africa, Asia, Latin America, the Caribbean, Oceania, or any other particular region.

However, applicants must still satisfy the academic eligibility requirements and all other programme conditions.

Applicants With or Without Current Academic Positions

Candidates may apply whether or not they currently hold a permanent full-time research or teaching position.

The programme therefore welcomes eligible scholars who:

  • Are currently completing their doctorate
  • Have recently completed a doctorate
  • Are working in temporary academic positions
  • Are working in research positions
  • Do not currently hold a permanent full-time academic position

This makes the fellowship particularly relevant to researchers at an early stage of their academic careers.

Who Is Not Eligible?

There are important exclusions that applicants should understand before preparing an application.

The following candidates are not eligible:

Current Postdoctoral Scholars at the University of Notre Dame

Current postdoctoral scholars at Notre Dame are not eligible to apply.

Doctoral Candidates and Graduates of the University of Notre Dame

Doctoral candidates at the University of Notre Dame and graduates of Notre Dame are also not eligible.

Applicants should carefully review these restrictions before investing time in preparing their application.

Participating Academic Units

The eight fellows selected for the 2027–2029 cohort will be distributed among eight participating units.

Department of Art, Art History, and Design

This unit provides opportunities for research relating to art, art history, design, visual culture, and related interdisciplinary areas.

Department of English

Applicants whose research focuses on literature, language, literary studies, cultural studies, or related areas may find potential alignment with this department.

Department of German, Slavic, and Eurasian Studies

This unit supports scholarship related to German, Slavic, Eurasian, linguistic, literary, historical, and cultural fields.

Department of Philosophy

Philosophy applicants may propose projects relating to areas such as ethics, epistemology, metaphysics, political philosophy, philosophy of science, or other relevant philosophical fields.

Department of Romance Languages and Literatures

This unit offers an academic home for research involving Romance languages, literatures, cultures, and related fields.

Department of Theology

Applicants conducting theological, religious, historical, ethical, or related research may consider the Department of Theology where their project aligns with its areas of expertise.

Initiative on Race and Resilience

This initiative provides opportunities for interdisciplinary research addressing questions related to race, resilience, society, history, culture, and related areas.

Program in History and Philosophy of Science

Researchers working at the intersection of history, philosophy, science, technology, and related fields may find alignment with this programme.

Application Requirements

Applicants must submit a complete application through Interfolio.

The application consists of several important components.

1. Cover Letter

Applicants must provide a cover letter explaining:

  • Their research trajectory
  • Their motivation for applying
  • How the fellowship would further their career goals

The cover letter must:

  • Be no more than 4 pages
  • Be double-spaced
  • Use 12-point font
  • Use 1-inch margins

Applicants should use the cover letter to present a clear narrative connecting their academic background, research trajectory, proposed fellowship plans, and long-term career goals.

2. Curriculum Vitae

Applicants must submit a CV documenting their academic and professional background.

The CV should clearly demonstrate relevant achievements such as:

  • Academic qualifications
  • Research experience
  • Publications
  • Conference presentations
  • Teaching experience
  • Grants
  • Awards
  • Fellowships
  • Professional activities
  • Other scholarly accomplishments

Because the selection process considers the applicant’s academic profile, candidates should ensure that their CV presents their strongest scholarly achievements clearly.

3. Research Statement

Applicants must submit a research statement describing:

  • Previous research accomplishments
  • Proposed research project or projects during the fellowship
  • The significance of the proposed work
  • Potential contribution of the research
  • Potential faculty mentors
  • Reasons for selecting potential mentors

The research statement must not exceed:

5 pages

It must also be:

  • Double-spaced
  • Written in 12-point font
  • Formatted with 1-inch margins

The research statement is one of the most important parts of the application because it allows the selection committee to evaluate the applicant’s scholarly trajectory and proposed research.

4. Writing Sample

Applicants must submit a writing sample representative of their own scholarly work.

The writing sample must not exceed:

10,000 words

Applicants should select a piece of work that demonstrates their strongest research, analytical, writing, and scholarly abilities.

5. Letters of Recommendation

Applicants must arrange for at least three letters of recommendation.

The recommendation letters must be submitted through Interfolio.

Applicants should not ask recommenders to email their letters directly to the University.

All required letters must be received by the application deadline.

Applications without the complete required number of recommendation letters will not be reviewed.

Applicants should therefore contact their recommenders well before the deadline to give them sufficient time to prepare and submit their letters.

Interfolio Application System

The University of Notre Dame is using Interfolio’s Faculty Search to manage the application process.

Applicants receive a free Dossier account through the application system.

This allows applicants to submit their application materials and confidential recommendation letters through the platform without paying a separate dossier fee.

Applicants should ensure that all materials are properly uploaded and that their recommenders have sufficient time to submit their letters before the deadline.

Application Deadline

December 1, 2026, at 11:59 PM Eastern Time

This is the official application deadline for the 2027–2029 Provost’s Postdoctoral Fellowship Program.

Applicants should submit their materials well before the deadline and should not wait until the final day, particularly because recommendation letters must also be submitted by the deadline.

Decision Date

Applicants are expected to receive fellowship decisions by:

March 1, 2027

The selection process will determine which candidates advance to the final cohort of eight fellows.

READ MORE HERE

How to Apply

Interested candidates should prepare their application materials and submit them through the University of Notre Dame’s Interfolio application portal HERE .

Applicants should ensure that the following are submitted:

  1. Cover letter
  2. Curriculum vitae
  3. Research statement
  4. Writing sample of no more than 10,000 words
  5. At least three letters of recommendation through Interfolio

All materials should be complete before the deadline.

Important Application Instructions

Applicants should pay close attention to the formatting requirements.

Cover Letter

Maximum of 4 pages, double-spaced, 12-point font, 1-inch margins.

Research Statement

Maximum of 5 pages, double-spaced, 12-point font, 1-inch margins.

Writing Sample

Maximum of 10,000 words.

Recommendation Letters

At least three letters must be submitted through Interfolio.

Mentor Contact

Applicants should not contact potential faculty mentors in the hosting department or institute to arrange mentorship before applying.

Instead, applicants can identify potential mentors in their research statement and explain why their expertise would benefit the proposed project.

Application Timeline

Milestone Date
Application opens August 3, 2026
Application deadline December 1, 2026, 11:59 PM ET
Fellowship decisions By March 1, 2027
Fellowship period 2027–2029 academic years

Equal Opportunity and Diversity

The University of Notre Dame states that it is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

The University does not discriminate on the basis of:

  • Race
  • Color
  • National origin
  • Ethnic origin
  • Sex
  • Disability
  • Veteran status
  • Genetic information
  • Age

The University also prohibits discrimination against qualified veterans and individuals with disabilities.

The institution encourages applicants who are attracted to a university with a Catholic identity.

Background Check

The appointment is contingent upon successful completion of a background check.

Applicants may be asked to identify:

  • Felony convictions
  • Pending felony charges

The University states that a felony conviction does not automatically prevent employment. Each case is considered individually to determine the appropriateness of employment.

Applicants are expected to provide truthful and complete information during the process.

Failure to disclose relevant information or dishonesty concerning required disclosures may result in disqualification.

Why This Fellowship Is Valuable for Early-Career Scholars

The Provost’s Postdoctoral Fellowship provides a combination of financial support, research development, faculty mentorship, professional development, and interdisciplinary engagement.

The programme can help fellows:

  • Develop an independent research agenda
  • Strengthen their publication record
  • Gain additional teaching experience
  • Develop grant-writing skills
  • Work with established faculty mentors
  • Build academic networks
  • Participate in interdisciplinary research
  • Present their work to academic audiences
  • Develop long-term career strategies
  • Strengthen their competitiveness for future academic positions

The two-year structure also gives fellows time to move beyond simply completing a short-term research project and instead build a sustainable academic research trajectory.

Application Checklist

Before submitting an application, candidates should confirm that they have:

  • Completed or will complete a doctoral degree between June 2024 and June 2027
  • Confirmed that they are not a current Notre Dame postdoctoral scholar
  • Confirmed that they are not a Notre Dame doctoral candidate or graduate
  • Prepared a cover letter of no more than 4 pages
  • Prepared their curriculum vitae
  • Prepared a research statement of no more than 5 pages
  • Selected a writing sample of no more than 10,000 words
  • Identified potential faculty mentors where appropriate
  • Explained the relevance of the proposed mentorship
  • Arranged at least three recommendation letters
  • Ensured recommenders submit their letters through Interfolio
  • Reviewed the relevant hosting unit
  • Reviewed potential interdisciplinary research opportunities
  • Submitted the complete application through Interfolio
  • Completed the application before December 1, 2026, at 11:59 PM ET

Frequently Important Questions

Is the fellowship open to international applicants?

Yes. The University explicitly states that scholars of all nationalities may apply.

What degree is required?

Applicants must have completed or plan to complete a doctoral degree within the specified eligibility period.

Can someone who has not yet completed their PhD apply?

Yes. Applicants who plan to complete their doctoral degree by June 2027 may apply.

Can applicants who already have full-time academic positions apply?

Yes. The programme welcomes candidates both with and without permanent full-time research or teaching positions, provided they meet the other eligibility requirements.

How many fellows will be selected?

The College of Arts & Letters plans to appoint eight postdoctoral fellows for the 2027–2029 academic years.

How long is the fellowship?

The fellowship is a two-year appointment.

What is the salary?

The annual salary is $75,000.

Is there additional research funding?

Yes. Fellows receive an additional $15,000 per year for research endeavors and further training.

How many recommendation letters are required?

At least three letters of recommendation must be submitted through Interfolio.

Can recommenders email their letters directly?

No. Applicants are instructed to have recommendation letters submitted through Interfolio, rather than emailed directly.

What is the application deadline?

The deadline is December 1, 2026, at 11:59 PM Eastern Time.

When will decisions be announced?

Decisions are expected by March 1, 2027.

Conclusion

The University of Notre Dame Provost’s Postdoctoral Fellowship Program 2027–2029 represents a significant opportunity for exceptional early-career scholars seeking to strengthen their academic careers through research, mentorship, interdisciplinary collaboration, and professional development.

The programme will select eight fellows for two-year appointments within the College of Arts & Letters. Fellows will receive a $75,000 annual salary, an additional $15,000 per year for research and training expenses, office space, faculty mentorship, and access to a university-wide community of distinguished researchers.

The fellowship is open to scholars of all nationalities, making it an internationally accessible opportunity for qualified researchers. However, applicants must satisfy the doctoral-degree eligibility window and should carefully note that current Notre Dame postdoctoral scholars, Notre Dame doctoral candidates, and Notre Dame doctoral graduates are not eligible.

Candidates interested in the fellowship should begin preparing their application well in advance. Particular attention should be given to the four-page cover letter, five-page research statement, 10,000-word writing sample, CV, and minimum of three recommendation letters.

The final application deadline is December 1, 2026, at 11:59 PM Eastern Time, with decisions expected by March 1, 2027.

For early-career scholars with an ambitious research agenda and a desire to participate in a highly interdisciplinary academic environment, the Notre Dame Provost’s Postdoctoral Fellowship offers an opportunity to develop scholarly expertise while building the foundation for a successful long-term academic career.

item.content:encoded:
Are you a final-year student studying Graphic Design, Digital Media, Visual Communication or a related discipline? Are you an African Union national currently residing in Ghana and looking for an opportunity to gain practical experience in an international organization? The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Secretariat Graphic Designer Internship 2026 offers eligible students an opportunity to gain hands-on professional experience while contributing to the communication and visual identity of one of the African Union’s flagship initiatives. The internship is designed to introduce talented and motivated African students to the work of the AfCFTA Secretariat and provide them with practical exposure to an international, multicultural working environment. As a Graphic Designer Intern, the successful candidate will contribute to the creation of visual communication materials for digital platforms, events, campaigns and publications. The role is particularly relevant to students who want to build professional experience in graphic design while working within an African Union institution.

Applications must be submitted online no later than 14 August 2026 at 11:59 p.m. UTC.

About the African Continental Free Trade Area

The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) is one of the flagship projects of the African Union’s Agenda 2063: The Africa We Want. It represents an ambitious effort to transform trade and economic cooperation across the African continent by creating a single continental market. The AfCFTA brings together the 55 Member States of the African Union and eight Regional Economic Communities (RECs). The initiative seeks to establish a continental market serving a population of approximately 1.3 billion people, with a combined gross domestic product of approximately US$3.4 trillion. Its broader objective is to facilitate the movement of goods and services across Africa while strengthening the continent’s position in global trade. By reducing barriers to intra-African trade and encouraging greater economic integration, the AfCFTA is intended to contribute to Africa’s long-term economic transformation.

About the AfCFTA Internship Programme

The AfCFTA Secretariat internship programme provides students with an opportunity to gain practical experience and international exposure in an institutional environment. The programme is intended for students who possess relevant knowledge and skills and are interested in learning how an important African Union initiative operates. The internship is primarily educational. Rather than simply providing students with an opportunity to observe professional activities, the programme is designed to expose interns to actual work carried out by the Secretariat and allow them to develop practical and professional skills. Successful interns can gain experience working in a multicultural environment while contributing to projects connected to the strategic priorities of the AfCFTA Secretariat.

Why the Graphic Designer Internship Is Important

Visual communication plays an increasingly important role in explaining complex international policy initiatives to the public. The AfCFTA works on issues involving trade, economic integration, development and Africa’s position in the global economy. Communicating these issues effectively requires professional visual materials that can reach different audiences through digital platforms, publications, events and campaigns. The Graphic Designer Intern will therefore have an important role in supporting the Secretariat’s communication activities. The position involves helping create visually compelling materials that communicate the work and ambitions of the AfCFTA. Through professional layout design, consistent branding and multimedia development, the intern will help strengthen the visual identity of the Secretariat and contribute to communicating AfCFTA’s work to different audiences.

Objectives of the AfCFTA Internship Programme

The internship programme has several major objectives.

1. Exposure to the Work of the AfCFTA Secretariat

The programme gives students an opportunity to become familiar with the work carried out by the AfCFTA Secretariat.

This exposure can help students understand how an international and continental institution operates and how professional teams contribute to broader development objectives.

2. Providing a Learning Platform

The internship is intended to serve as a learning platform for qualified students. Participants can apply knowledge gained through their academic programmes to practical tasks while developing additional technical and professional abilities.

3. First-Hand Experience With an African Union Flagship Project

The programme gives students the opportunity to experience, first-hand, the work of one of the African Union’s ambitious projects. This can help bridge the gap between academic education and professional experience.

4. Encouraging Young Africans to Pursue International Careers

The programme also aims to promote the AfCFTA to the general public, particularly young people, and encourage them to work toward their aspirations of contributing to international organizations. For students interested in careers involving international development, African integration, policy, communications or international organizations, the internship can provide an introduction to this professional environment.

Who Can Apply for the AfCFTA Graphic Designer Internship?

Eligibility is an important part of this opportunity.

Applicants must satisfy the requirements established by the AfCFTA Secretariat.

1. African Union Nationality and Residence in Ghana

Applicants must:

  • Be nationals of a Member State of the African Union; and
  • Be residing in Ghana.

This means that the opportunity is specifically targeted at African Union nationals who are currently residing in Ghana. Being an African national alone does not satisfy the full eligibility requirement if the applicant does not meet the stated residence requirement.

2. Final-Year Student Status

Applicants must be final-year students. They must be enrolled on a full-time basis in a fully accredited degree programme at a recognized public or private institution of higher learning.

The applicant’s field of study should be:

  • Graphic Design
  • Digital Media
  • Visual Communication
  • A related field

Students from closely related disciplines should carefully consider whether their academic programme fits the requirements before submitting an application.

3. Availability for the Internship

Applicants must have full availability for a minimum of three months, which is the stated duration requirement for the programme.

Students should therefore ensure that their academic, personal or professional commitments will not prevent them from participating fully in the internship.

4. Language Skills

Applicants must have proficiency in at least one of the African Union’s official working languages.

These include:

  • French
  • English
  • Portuguese
  • Arabic
  • Kiswahili
  • Spanish

Fluency in another AU language is considered an added advantage.

Strong communication skills are particularly important for a graphic design position because the intern may need to collaborate with colleagues, understand project requirements and develop visual materials for different audiences.

5. Graphic Design and Visual Communication Skills

Applicants should be capable of developing visuals for different types of media.

The required capabilities include creating visual materials for:

  • Digital campaigns
  • Websites
  • Print production
  • Other communication platforms

Applicants should therefore have an understanding of how design requirements differ across digital and physical formats.

6. Design Software Skills

Applicants should have proficiency in industry-standard design software, including:

  • Adobe Illustrator
  • Adobe Photoshop
  • Adobe InDesign
  • Adobe After Effects

Knowledge of video editing tools, particularly Adobe Premiere Pro, is considered an advantage.

Applicants with experience combining graphic design, motion graphics and video editing may therefore have an additional skill relevant to the position.

7. Ability to Work in a Multicultural Environment

The successful candidate should be capable and willing to work in a multicultural and international team environment.

This is particularly important because the AfCFTA is a continental initiative involving countries and stakeholders from across Africa.

The internship therefore requires more than technical design skills. Candidates should also be comfortable communicating and collaborating with people from different professional, cultural and national backgrounds.

8. Commitment to Institutional Values

Applicants must be committed to upholding and adhering to the rules and values of the institution throughout the internship programme. This means successful interns will be expected to conduct themselves professionally and respect the standards governing work within the AfCFTA Secretariat.

9. Female Candidates Are Encouraged to Apply

The AfCFTA specifically states that female candidates are encouraged to apply. Qualified female students who meet the eligibility requirements are therefore strongly encouraged to consider this opportunity.

What Will the Graphic Designer Intern Do?

The Graphic Designer Intern will support the creation of visual communication materials for the AfCFTA Secretariat.

The role can involve contributing to materials intended for:

  • Digital platforms
  • Events
  • Campaigns
  • Publications
  • Other communication activities

The intern’s work will contribute to maintaining a coherent visual identity for the Secretariat and communicating its activities and priorities effectively.

Digital Communication

Digital communication is an important component of modern institutional communication. The intern may contribute to visual content intended for online platforms and digital campaigns. This requires an understanding of how design principles can be adapted to digital audiences and different screen formats.

Event Materials

The intern may also support the development of visual materials associated with AfCFTA events. This could require applying consistent branding and creating professional layouts that align with the organization’s communication standards.

Publications

Graphic design is also important in institutional publications. The intern may contribute to layouts and visual elements that make reports and other publications clear, professional and accessible.

Branding Consistency

Another important part of the role is maintaining consistency in the Secretariat’s visual identity. Consistent use of design elements helps an organization communicate professionally across multiple platforms and publications.

Multimedia Development

The role also includes a multimedia dimension. Knowledge of After Effects is specifically required, while knowledge of Premiere Pro is an advantage. This indicates that applicants may benefit from having skills extending beyond static graphic design into motion graphics and video production.

How to Apply for the AfCFTA Internship

Applications for the AfCFTA Secretariat Internship Programme are submitted online. Applicants should carefully follow the registration and application instructions.

Step 1: Register on the Online Recruitment System

If you are using the online registration system for the first time, you will need to create an account before logging in.

Applicants should make sure that the information entered during registration is accurate and complete.

Step 2: Complete Your Application

Applicants are advised to provide as much relevant information as possible when completing their online application.

Relevant academic, professional, technical and personal information should be presented accurately.

Step 3: Prepare the Required Supporting Documents

Applicants must submit the required supporting documentation with their online application.

The listed documents include:

Motivation Letter

Applicants must provide a motivation letter addressed to the Administration and Human Resources Directorate of the Secretariat.

The letter should indicate what the applicant expects to gain from the internship programme.

A well-prepared motivation letter should therefore clearly communicate the applicant’s genuine interest in the internship and explain their learning objectives.

Valid Passport or Identity Card

Applicants must submit a copy of a valid:

  • Passport; or
  • Identity card

The document should be valid and legible.

Current Curriculum Vitae

Applicants must also provide a current CV.

The CV should accurately reflect the applicant’s academic background, design experience, technical skills and other relevant qualifications.

Application Confirmation

After successfully submitting the application, applicants will receive an email confirmation stating that their application has been received. Applicants should keep this confirmation for their records. If an applicant does not receive confirmation after submitting an application, they should check their email and application account and ensure that the submission was completed successfully.

TO LEARN AND APPLY CLICK HERE

Selection Process

The AfCFTA internship selection process consists of four main stages.

Stage 1: Pre-Screening

All submitted applications are screened.

Candidates who meet the relevant requirements may be placed on a shortlist that is made available to AfCFTA Secretariat Directorates.

This means that submitting an application does not automatically guarantee progression to the next stage.

Stage 2: Interview and/or Written Test

Hiring teams may invite shortlisted candidates to participate in:

  • A telephone interview
  • A written test
  • Both an interview and written test, where applicable

Candidates should therefore be prepared to demonstrate both their technical abilities and their understanding of the internship.

For a Graphic Designer Intern position, applicants should also be prepared to discuss their design experience, software skills, creative approach and ability to work within professional requirements.

Stage 3: Offer Letter

A candidate who is selected will receive an email containing an internship offer letter from the Administration and Human Resources Management Directorate (AHRM Directorate).

Applicants should monitor the email address associated with their application after submission.

Stage 4: References

Verifiable references may be required.

Applicants should therefore be prepared to provide reliable references if requested during the recruitment process.

Terms and Conditions of the Internship

Applicants should carefully understand the financial and administrative conditions associated with the internship.

No Financial Obligation Toward Interns

The AfCFTA Secretariat states that it will have no financial obligation towards interns.

This is an important condition that applicants should consider before applying.

Travel, Accommodation and Living Costs

Travel arrangements and the costs associated with:

  • Accommodation
  • Living expenses
  • Travel

will be the responsibility of the interns.

Applicants should therefore ensure that they understand and can manage the financial implications of participating in the programme.

No Travel Compensation

Interns will not be entitled to compensation for travel.

Prospective applicants should take this into account when evaluating whether they can participate in the internship.

Internship Authorization and Duration

The terms and conditions state that the internship will be authorized initially for six months, with the possibility of one renewal.

The information provided also states that interns may have the possibility of rotating to another department.

Confirmation of interns for each period will depend solely on business needs.

Applicants should therefore understand that continuation or placement arrangements are subject to institutional requirements.

Important Deadline for Applicants

The application deadline is:

14 August 2026 at 11:59 p.m. UTC.

Applicants should submit their applications before the stated closing time.

Because online applications may require registration, document preparation and submission of supporting materials, prospective applicants should avoid waiting until the final hours to complete the process.

Important Application Considerations

Before submitting an application, prospective candidates should carefully check the following:

  1. Confirm that you are a national of an African Union Member State.
  2. Confirm that you are residing in Ghana.
  3. Confirm that you are a final-year student.
  4. Confirm that you are studying Graphic Design, Digital Media, Visual Communication or a related discipline.
  5. Confirm that your degree programme is full-time and fully accredited.
  6. Confirm that your institution is recognized.
  7. Make sure you can commit to the required internship period.
  8. Review your proficiency in the AU working languages.
  9. Ensure that your graphic design portfolio and skills demonstrate competence across relevant media formats.
  10. Review your proficiency in Illustrator, Photoshop, InDesign and After Effects.
  11. Highlight Premiere Pro or other video editing experience if applicable.
  12. Prepare a clear motivation letter.
  13. Prepare a current CV.
  14. Ensure that your passport or identity card is valid.
  15. Complete the online registration process if you are a first-time user.
  16. Submit all required documents.
  17. Keep a copy of your application and confirmation email.
  18. Submit the application before 14 August 2026 at 11:59 p.m. UTC.

Who Would Benefit Most From This Internship?

This opportunity may be particularly relevant to final-year students who want to build a career in areas such as:

  • Graphic design
  • Digital communications
  • Visual communication
  • Multimedia production
  • International organizations
  • Public-sector communications
  • Development communications
  • African regional institutions
  • International development
  • Corporate communications
  • Policy communications
  • Creative media

Students who want to combine creative skills with international affairs and development-related work may find the placement especially relevant.

Building a Career Through Practical Experience

One of the major purposes of the internship is to help students move from academic learning toward professional experience.

University education can provide students with theoretical knowledge and technical foundations, but professional environments require additional capabilities such as:

  • Meeting deadlines
  • Working within organizational guidelines
  • Collaborating with colleagues
  • Responding to feedback
  • Managing multiple tasks
  • Communicating professionally
  • Producing work for real audiences
  • Adapting designs to institutional requirements

An internship at the AfCFTA Secretariat can provide an environment in which students begin developing these professional habits.

Understanding the Broader African Context

The internship is also situated within the broader objectives of African economic integration.

The AfCFTA is intended to strengthen trade and economic cooperation among African countries and contribute to the continent’s long-term development ambitions.

For a Graphic Designer, this creates an opportunity to work on communication that is connected to major continental issues.

The intern’s creative work can therefore form part of a wider effort to communicate the AfCFTA’s objectives and activities to audiences across Africa and internationally.

Conclusion

The AfCFTA Graphic Designer Internship 2026 in Ghana offers eligible final-year students an opportunity to gain practical experience within the Secretariat of the African Continental Free Trade Area, one of the flagship initiatives of the African Union’s Agenda 2063. The internship is particularly suited to students studying Graphic Design, Digital Media, Visual Communication or related disciplines who have strong technical abilities in tools such as Adobe Illustrator, Photoshop, InDesign and After Effects. The role focuses on visual communication and can involve creating materials for digital platforms, campaigns, events and publications while supporting the visual identity and communication objectives of the AfCFTA Secretariat. Applicants must be nationals of an African Union Member State and residing in Ghana, must be final-year full-time students at recognized institutions, and must meet the specified academic, technical, language and professional requirements. Female candidates are specifically encouraged to apply. Applicants should also carefully consider the financial conditions of the programme. The AfCFTA Secretariat states that it has no financial obligation towards interns, while travel, accommodation and living expenses are the responsibility of the interns. The selection process may include pre-screening, an interview and/or written test, followed by an offer letter for successful candidates. Verifiable references may also be requested.Most importantly, applications must be submitted online no later than 14 August 2026 at 11:59 p.m. UTC. Eligible students interested in developing their graphic design and communication careers while gaining exposure to an important African Union initiative should carefully review the requirements, prepare the required documents and submit their application before the deadline.
